Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?\"**\r\n\r\n**If Subagent-driven chosen:**\r\n- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development\r\n\r\n**If Native chosen:**\r\n- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans\r\n# Writing Good Tests\r\n\r\n**Load this reference when:** writing or changing tests, adding mocks, or\r\nadding cleanup/helper methods for tests.\r\n\r\n## Overview\r\n\r\nA test exists to catch a specific break. Two principles govern everything\r\nhere:\r\n\r\n```\r\n1. Every test names the break it catches\r\n2. Every test exercises the real thing\r\n```\r\n\r\nStrict TDD produces both naturally: a test written first and watched\r\nfailing against real code has already proven it can fail, and only earns\r\na mock when the real dependency proves slow or external.\r\n\r\n## Principle 1: Name the Break\r\n\r\nBefore writing the test body, answer: **what production change should\r\nmake this test fail — and is that change a bug or a decision?** A test\r\nearns its place by catching a wrong branch, missing side effect, wrong\r\nargument, boundary case, or broken contract.\r\n\r\n**Derive expectations independently.** Use literals and hand-checked\r\nfixtures; table-driven tests with literal `want` values are the preferred\r\nshape. An expectation computed by the code under test — or its helpers —\r\npasses no matter what that code does:\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// ❌ Mirror assertion: the same builder computes both sides — always true\r\nconst expected = buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' });\r\nexpect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe(expected);\r\n\r\n// ✅ Hand-derived literal\r\nexpect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe('tag:\"urgent\"');\r\n```\r\n\r\n**No change detectors.** If only intentional decisions can fail a test —\r\na constant's value, exact message wording, private structure — it fires\r\non redesign and sleeps through bugs. Test the behavior that depends on\r\nthe decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but \"a failing call is\r\nretried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens.\"\r\n\r\n**Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config\r\ncontains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run\r\nscripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or\r\nexit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming\r\nagent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no\r\ntest at all.\r\n\r\n**Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at\r\nits boundaries — the route you register, the query you emit, the payload\r\nyou produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write\r\n(the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler — that\r\nis the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely\r\nsurprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the\r\nassumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,\r\ngetters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they\r\nvalidate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects —\r\notherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.\r\n\r\n### Gate Function\r\n\r\n```\r\nBEFORE writing the test body:\r\n  Name the production change that would make this test fail.\r\n\r\n  Cannot name one            → redesign around an observable behavior\r\n  \"The source text changed\"  → run the artifact and assert its effects\r\n  Only intentional decisions → change detector; test the behavior\r\n                               that depends on the decision\r\n\r\n  Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.\r\n  IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:\r\n    Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Principle 2: Exercise the Real Thing\r\n\r\n**The mock earns no assertions.** A mock assertion passes when the mock\r\nis present and fails when it is absent — it says nothing about the\r\ncomponent. Assert the real component's behavior; if the mock is what you\r\nare checking, unmock it or delete the assertion.\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// ✅ Real behavior\r\nexpect(screen.getByRole('navigation')).toBeInTheDocument();\r\n\r\n// ❌ Mock existence\r\nexpect(screen.getByTestId('sidebar-mock')).toBeInTheDocument();\r\n```\r\n\r\n**your human partner's correction:** \"Are we testing the behavior of a\r\nmock?\"\r\n\r\n**Mock at the right level.** Learn every side effect of the real method\r\nbefore replacing it; mock the slow or external operation and keep what\r\nthe test depends on real. When unsure, run the test against the real\r\nimplementation first and observe what actually needs to happen.\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// ❌ The mock swallows the config write that duplicate detection reads\r\nvi.mock('ToolCatalog', () => ({\r\n  discoverAndCacheTools: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined)\r\n}));\r\n\r\n// ✅ Mock only the slow server startup; the config write stays real\r\nvi.mock('MCPServerManager');\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Make doubles specific.** When arguments, call counts, or ordering are\r\npart of the contract, assert them — a fake that accepts anything verifies\r\nnothing. Give each branch (success, error, malformed) its own fixture or\r\nspy, so the wrong branch cannot satisfy the expectation.\r\n\r\n**Mirror real data completely.** Mock the complete structure as it exists\r\nin reality — all documented fields — not just the ones your test reads.\r\nPartial mocks fail silently when downstream code reads an omitted field:\r\nthe test passes while integration breaks.\r\n\r\n**Production classes carry production methods only.** Cleanup that only\r\ntests need lives in test utilities, never as a `destroy()` on the\r\nproduction class. Ask: is this method called only from tests? Does this\r\nclass own this resource's lifecycle? Wrong answers → test utility.\r\n\r\n**Prefer real components over complex mocks.** When mock setup outgrows\r\nthe test logic, mocks miss methods the real components have, or tests\r\nbreak when the mock changes, switch to an integration test with real\r\ncomponents. **your human partner's question:** \"Do we need to be using a\r\nmock here?\"\r\n\r\n### Gate Function\r\n\r\n```\r\nBEFORE adding a mock or test helper:\r\n  List the real method's side effects; keep the ones the test\r\n  depends on real — mock the slow/external level below them.\r\n\r\n  Mock responses mirror the complete real structure.\r\n\r\n  A method only tests call lives in test utilities, not production.\r\n\r\n  About to assert on the mock itself?\r\n    Unmock it or delete the assertion.\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Tests Ship With the Implementation\r\n\r\nThe TDD cycle — failing test, minimal implementation, refactor — is what\r\n\"complete\" means. Ship the tests the behavior needs and only those:\r\ntrivial code and human prose earn none, and a test written to satisfy\r\nprocess costs maintenance forever.\r\n\r\n## The Mutation Check\r\n\r\nBefore finishing, mentally mutate the production code; at least one test\r\nshould fail for each realistic mutation:\r\n\r\n- Wrong constant or argument\r\n- Wrong branch handler\r\n- Missing state change or side effect\r\n- Empty or default return\r\n- Missing validation for zero, empty, nil, unauthorized, or malformed input\r\n\r\nA mutation nothing catches marks the behavior as unprotected — or the\r\ntest as tautological.\r\n\r\n## Quick Reference\r\n\r\n| When you... | Do |\r\n|-------------|-----|\r\n| Write any test | Name the break it catches — a bug, not a decision |\r\n| Build an expected value | Derive it by hand; never with the code under test |\r\n| Test a script or document | Run it / pressure-test its consumer; never grep its text |\r\n| Reach for a dependency test | Test your boundary contract, not their documented mechanics |\r\n| Want to assert on a mocked element | Test the real component, or unmock it |\r\n| Are about to mock a method | Learn its side effects; mock the slow/external level |\r\n| Build a mock response | Mirror the real structure completely |\r\n| Need cleanup only tests use | Put it in test utilities |\r\n| Watch mock setup balloon | Switch to an integration test with real components |\r\n| Finish a test file | Run the mutation check |\r\n\r\n## Warning Signs\r\n\r\n- Setup and assertion share the same object, guaranteeing equality\r\n- The test can fail only through a panic, crash, or missing selector\r\n- The test fails on every intentional change, never on accidental breakage\r\n- Expected values are hidden behind loops, builders, or helpers\r\n- The test greps source text, or asserts a removed symbol stays removed\r\n- The test would still matter if only the framework remained\r\n- The test exists for coverage, checking no side effect or outcome\r\n- An assertion checks a `*-mock` test ID, or fails if you remove the mock\r\n- A method is called only from test files\r\n- Mock setup is more than half the test, or you can't explain why the mock is needed\r\n- Mocking \"just to be safe\"\r\n", "exit_code": 0, "duration": {"secs": 0, "nanos": 659684600}}, "started_at_ms": 1794676290061, "completed_at_ms": 1794676290724}}

Remote deployment requires the user's explicit subsequent approval.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: writing-plans\\r\\ndescription: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Writing Plans\\r\\n\\r\\n## Overview\\r\\n\\r\\nWrite implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Announce at start:** \\\"I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan.\\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`\\r\\n- (User preferences for plan location override this default)\\r\\n\\r\\n## Scope Check\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.\\r\\n\\r\\n## File Structure\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.\\r\\n\\r\\n- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.\\r\\n- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.\\r\\n- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.\\r\\n- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Task Right-Sizing\\r\\n\\r\\nA task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a\\r\\nfresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,\\r\\nconfiguration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose\\r\\ndeliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully\\r\\nreject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an\\r\\nindependently testable deliverable.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Step Granularity\\r\\n\\r\\n**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**\\r\\n- \\\"Write the failing test\\\" - step\\r\\n- \\\"Run it to make sure it fails\\\" - step\\r\\n- \\\"Implement the minimal code to make the test pass\\\" - step\\r\\n- \\\"Run the tests and make sure they pass\\\" - step\\r\\n- \\\"Commit\\\" - step\\r\\n\\r\\n## Plan Document Header\\r\\n\\r\\n**Every plan MUST start with this header:**\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\n# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan\\r\\n\\r\\n> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]\\r\\n\\r\\n**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]\\r\\n\\r\\n**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]\\r\\n\\r\\n**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan\\r\\nargues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]\\r\\n\\r\\n## Global Constraints\\r\\n\\r\\n[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,\\r\\nnaming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact\\r\\nvalues copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly\\r\\ninclude this section.]\\r\\n\\r\\n## Review Focus\\r\\n\\r\\n[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's\\r\\ntests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software\\r\\n— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a\\r\\nreasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision\\r\\ndocument: it says what the software must do, not everything it will\\r\\nmeet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to\\r\\nbreak the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of\\r\\nyou. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that\\r\\nowns the code, in that task's own step style.]\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Task Structure\\r\\n\\r\\n````markdown\\r\\n### Task N: [Component Name]\\r\\n\\r\\n**Files:**\\r\\n- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`\\r\\n- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`\\r\\n- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`\\r\\n\\r\\n**Interfaces:**\\r\\n- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]\\r\\n- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter\\r\\n  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this\\r\\n  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**\\r\\n\\r\\n```python\\r\\ndef test_specific_behavior():\\r\\n    result = function(input)\\r\\n    assert result == expected\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**\\r\\n\\r\\nRun: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`\\r\\nExpected: FAIL with \\\"function not defined\\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**\\r\\n\\r\\nOne line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice\\r\\n(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an\\r\\nalgorithm they do not determine.\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**\\r\\n\\r\\nRun: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`\\r\\nExpected: PASS\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngit add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py\\r\\ngit commit -m \\\"feat: add specific feature\\\"\\r\\n```\\r\\n````\\r\\n\\r\\n## What a Step Contains\\r\\n\\r\\nA step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing\\r\\nfrom it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind\\r\\nof step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the\\r\\n  spec's exact values in them.\\r\\n- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the\\r\\n  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer\\r\\n  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and\\r\\n  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.\\r\\n- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it\\r\\n  passed.\\r\\n- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what\\r\\n  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.\\r\\n\\r\\nA plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan\\r\\nlonger than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that\\r\\ndecide nothing (\\\"TBD\\\", \\\"handle edge cases\\\", \\\"add appropriate validation\\\",\\r\\n\\\"write tests for the above\\\", a type or function no task defines) are the\\r\\nopposite failure, and the self-review catches both.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Self-Review\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.\\r\\n\\r\\n**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.\\r\\n\\r\\n**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.\\r\\n\\r\\n**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.\\r\\n\\r\\n**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.\\r\\n\\r\\n**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Execution Handoff\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner\\r\\nto read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask\\r\\nthem to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that\\r\\nreview before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask\\r\\nthem to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.\\r\\n\\r\\n**When no execution method has already been supplied:**\\r\\n\\r\\n**\\\"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Two principles govern everything\\r\\nhere:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n1. Every test names the break it catches\\r\\n2. Every test exercises the real thing\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nStrict TDD produces both naturally: a test written first and watched\\r\\nfailing against real code has already proven it can fail, and only earns\\r\\na mock when the real dependency proves slow or external.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Principle 1: Name the Break\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore writing the test body, answer: **what production change should\\r\\nmake this test fail — and is that change a bug or a decision?** A test\\r\\nearns its place by catching a wrong branch, missing side effect, wrong\\r\\nargument, boundary case, or broken contract.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Derive expectations independently.** Use literals and hand-checked\\r\\nfixtures; table-driven tests with literal `want` values are the preferred\\r\\nshape. An expectation computed by the code under test — or its helpers —\\r\\npasses no matter what that code does:\\r\\n\\r\\n```typescript\\r\\n// ❌ Mirror assertion: the same builder computes both sides — always true\\r\\nconst expected = buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' });\\r\\nexpect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe(expected);\\r\\n\\r\\n// ✅ Hand-derived literal\\r\\nexpect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe('tag:\\\"urgent\\\"');\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**No change detectors.** If only intentional decisions can fail a test —\\r\\na constant's value, exact message wording, private structure — it fires\\r\\non redesign and sleeps through bugs. Test the behavior that depends on\\r\\nthe decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but \\\"a failing call is\\r\\nretried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens.\\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config\\r\\ncontains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run\\r\\nscripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or\\r\\nexit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming\\r\\nagent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no\\r\\ntest at all.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at\\r\\nits boundaries — the route you register, the query you emit, the payload\\r\\nyou produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write\\r\\n(the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler — that\\r\\nis the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely\\r\\nsurprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the\\r\\nassumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,\\r\\ngetters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they\\r\\nvalidate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects —\\r\\notherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Gate Function\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nBEFORE writing the test body:\\r\\n  Name the production change that would make this test fail.\\r\\n\\r\\n  Cannot name one            → redesign around an observable behavior\\r\\n  \\\"The source text changed\\\"  → run the artifact and assert its effects\\r\\n  Only intentional decisions → change detector; test the behavior\\r\\n                               that depends on the decision\\r\\n\\r\\n  Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.\\r\\n  IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:\\r\\n    Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Principle 2: Exercise the Real Thing\\r\\n\\r\\n**The mock earns no assertions.** A mock assertion passes when the mock\\r\\nis present and fails when it is absent — it says nothing about the\\r\\ncomponent. Assert the real component's behavior; if the mock is what you\\r\\nare checking, unmock it or delete the assertion.\\r\\n\\r\\n```typescript\\r\\n// ✅ Real behavior\\r\\nexpect(screen.getByRole('navigation')).toBeInTheDocument();\\r\\n\\r\\n// ❌ Mock existence\\r\\nexpect(screen.getByTestId('sidebar-mock')).toBeInTheDocument();\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**your human partner's correction:** \\\"Are we testing the behavior of a\\r\\nmock?\\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**Mock at the right level.** Learn every side effect of the real method\\r\\nbefore replacing it; mock the slow or external operation and keep what\\r\\nthe test depends on real. When unsure, run the test against the real\\r\\nimplementation first and observe what actually needs to happen.\\r\\n\\r\\n```typescript\\r\\n// ❌ The mock swallows the config write that duplicate detection reads\\r\\nvi.mock('ToolCatalog', () => ({\\r\\n  discoverAndCacheTools: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined)\\r\\n}));\\r\\n\\r\\n// ✅ Mock only the slow server startup; the config write stays real\\r\\nvi.mock('MCPServerManager');\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Make doubles specific.** When arguments, call counts, or ordering are\\r\\npart of the contract, assert them — a fake that accepts anything verifies\\r\\nnothing. Give each branch (success, error, malformed) its own fixture or\\r\\nspy, so the wrong branch cannot satisfy the expectation.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Mirror real data completely.** Mock the complete structure as it exists\\r\\nin reality — all documented fields — not just the ones your test reads.\\r\\nPartial mocks fail silently when downstream code reads an omitted field:\\r\\nthe test passes while integration breaks.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Production classes carry production methods only.** Cleanup that only\\r\\ntests need lives in test utilities, never as a `destroy()` on the\\r\\nproduction class. at least one test\\r\\nshould fail for each realistic mutation:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Wrong constant or argument\\r\\n- Wrong branch handler\\r\\n- Missing state change or side effect\\r\\n- Empty or default return\\r\\n- Missing validation for zero, empty, nil, unauthorized, or malformed input\\r\\n\\r\\nA mutation nothing catches marks the behavior as unprotected — or the\\r\\ntest as tautological.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Quick Reference\\r\\n\\r\\n| When you... | Do |\\r\\n|-------------|-----|\\r\\n| Write any test | Name the break it catches — a bug, not a decision |\\r\\n| Build an expected value | Derive it by hand; Status: proposed for review; not approved for implementation.\r\n\r\nThe proposed application schema contains **four tables: `profiles`, `user_preferences`, `tasks`, and `events`**, alongside the existing, externally managed `auth.users`. It supports account/profile foundations, preferences, task inputs, individual fixed commitments, and repeating weekly university/work timetables. It does not create generated schedules or perform optimization.\r\n\r\nThe user clarified during this review that **weekly recurrence is required** and **task importance uses integers 1–5, with 5 most important**. These are explicit requirements for this proposal. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.\r\n\r\n**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.\r\n\r\n**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**\r\n\r\n## When to Use\r\n\r\n**Always:**\r\n- New features\r\n- Bug fixes\r\n- Refactoring\r\n- Behavior changes\r\n\r\n**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**\r\n- Throwaway prototypes\r\n- Generated code\r\n- Configuration files\r\n\r\nThinking \"skip TDD just this once\"? Stop. That's rationalization.\r\n\r\n## The Iron Law\r\n\r\n```\r\nNO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST\r\n```\r\n\r\nWrite code before the test? Delete it. Start over.\r\n\r\n**No exceptions:**\r\n- Don't keep it as \"reference\"\r\n- Don't \"adapt\" it while writing tests\r\n- Don't look at it\r\n- Delete means delete\r\n\r\nImplement fresh from tests. Period.\r\n\r\n## Red-Green-Refactor\r\n\r\n```dot\r\ndigraph tdd_cycle {\r\n    rankdir=LR;\r\n    red [label=\"RED\\nWrite failing test\", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor=\"#ffcccc\"];\r\n    verify_red [label=\"Verify fails\\ncorrectly\", shape=diamond];\r\n    green [label=\"GREEN\\nMinimal code\", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor=\"#ccffcc\"];\r\n    verify_green [label=\"Verify passes\\nAll green\", shape=diamond];\r\n    refactor [label=\"REFACTOR\\nClean up\", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor=\"#ccccff\"];\r\n    next [label=\"Next\", shape=ellipse];\r\n\r\n    red -> verify_red;\r\n    verify_red -> green [label=\"yes\"];\r\n    verify_red -> red [label=\"wrong\\nfailure\"];\r\n    green -> verify_green;\r\n    verify_green -> refactor [label=\"yes\"];\r\n    verify_green -> green [label=\"no\"];\r\n    refactor -> verify_green [label=\"stay\\ngreen\"];\r\n    verify_green -> next;\r\n    next -> red;\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### RED - Write Failing Test\r\n\r\nWrite one minimal test showing what should happen.\r\n\r\n<Good>\r\n```typescript\r\ntest('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {\r\n  let attempts = 0;\r\n  const operation = () => {\r\n    attempts++;\r\n    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');\r\n    return 'success';\r\n  };\r\n\r\n  const result = await retryOperation(operation);\r\n\r\n  expect(result).toBe('success');\r\n  expect(attempts).toBe(3);\r\n});\r\n```\r\nClear name, tests real behavior, one thing\r\n</Good>\r\n\r\n<Bad>\r\n```typescript\r\n", "exit_code": 0, "duration": {"secs": 0, "nanos": 548927700}}, "started_at_ms": 1794676317036, "completed_at_ms": 1794676317586}}

It supports account/profile foundations, preferences, task inputs, individual fixed commitments, and repeating weekly university/work timetables. It does not create generated schedules or perform optimization.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user clarified during this review that **weekly recurrence is required** and **task importance uses integers 1–5, with 5 most important**. These are explicit requirements for this proposal. All application tables are in `public`. `—` means no explicit database default; nullable fields are NULL when omitted. Unless stated otherwise, a non-key column has no uniqueness constraint. All listed PKs are unique and NOT NULL. Check names referenced in the tables are defined immediately after the corresponding table. Defaults and nullable profile fields are proposed onboarding choices, not source requirements.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse PostgreSQL `uuid`, `timestamptz`, `date`, `time(0) without time zone`, `boolean`, `integer`, and bounded `varchar` types. Named CHECK constraints on strings are proposed instead of native PostgreSQL ENUM types, so later approved vocabulary changes do not require ENUM surgery. The stored vocabulary is uppercase and matches the Master where applicable.\\r\\n\\r\\n**`profiles`** stores application identity details only. If end is earlier than start, the preference crosses midnight into the following day. Equal endpoints do not mean an implicit 24-hour interval. No work-hour default is inferred from the user's location or role.\\r\\n\\r\\n`timezone` is an IANA timezone name such as `Africa/Cairo`, or `UTC`. Do not put a subquery against that view into a CHECK. A table-reading validation function must not be declared IMMUTABLE merely to use it as a CHECK. The default UTC is a fallback until the user supplies their preference, not an assumption that they live in UTC.\\r\\n\\r\\n**`tasks`** stores work to complete. `priority` is the user's importance input, not a computed decision score. `context` provides the existing Master's optional task context/details without adding a second overlapping description field.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Column | PostgreSQL type | Key / reference | Nullability | Default | Unique / check |\\r\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\r\\n| task_id | uuid | PK | NOT NULL | gen_random_uuid() | PK |\\r\\n| user_id | uuid | FK → profiles(id) | NOT NULL | — | Owner |\\r\\n| title | varchar(500) | — | NOT NULL | — | T1 |\\r\\n| task_type | varchar(8) | — | NOT NULL | — | T2: FIXED or FLEXIBLE |\\r\\n| deadline | timestamptz | — | NULL | — | T3: finite when supplied |\\r\\n| estimated_duration_minutes | integer | — | NOT NULL | — | T4: greater than zero |\\r\\n| category | varchar(20) | — | NOT NULL | — | T5: approved category vocabulary |\\r\\n| priority | integer | — | NOT NULL | — | T6: BETWEEN 1 AND 5 |\\r\\n| fixed_start_at | timestamptz | — | NULL; Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**\\r\\n\\r\\n## When to Use\\r\\n\\r\\n**Always:**\\r\\n- New features\\r\\n- Bug fixes\\r\\n- Refactoring\\r\\n- Behavior changes\\r\\n\\r\\n**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**\\r\\n- Throwaway prototypes\\r\\n- Generated code\\r\\n- Configuration files\\r\\n\\r\\nThinking \\\"skip TDD just this once\\\"? Stop. That's rationalization.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The Iron Law\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nNO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWrite code before the test? Delete it. Swagger: `/docs`; ReDoc: `/redoc`; OpenAPI: `/openapi.json` and exported docs/openapi.json. Every operation includes request/response examples, validation and errors. No Flutter code or integration is included.\n\nPublic endpoints: health, register, login, refresh. All others require `Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN`. Never submit user_id, generated IDs, timestamps, task status, or event source/status. Obtain current user/profile identity from authenticated responses, not a request body.\n\n## Routes and contracts\n\n| Method | URL | Request/example | Success response |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| GET | `/health` | No body | 200 `{\"status\":\"ok\"}` |\n| GET | `/health/ready` | No body | 200 `{\"status\":\"ready\"}`; restricted DB/RLS check |\n| POST | `/auth/register` | Auth example below; optional username/full_name | 201 AuthResponse; session may be null for email confirmation |\n| POST | `/auth/login` | Email/password Auth example | 200 AuthResponse |\n| POST | `/auth/refresh` | `{\"refresh_token\":\"REFRESH_TOKEN\"}` | 200 AuthResponse with rotated session |\n| GET | `/profiles/me` | Bearer, no body | 200 ProfileRead; missing own profile provisioned idempotently |\n| PATCH | `/profiles/me` | `{\"full_name\":\"Student Name\"}` | 200 updated ProfileRead |\n| GET | `/preferences/me` | Bearer, no body | 200 PreferencesRead |\n| PATCH | `/preferences/me` | Preferences example below | 200 updated PreferencesRead |\n| POST | `/tasks` | Task example below | 201 TaskRead |\n| GET | `/tasks` | `?limit=50&offset=0&category=STUDY` | 200 Page of TaskRead |\n| GET | `/tasks/{task_id}` | UUID path, no body | 200 TaskRead |\n| PATCH | `/tasks/{task_id}` | `{\"priority\":5}` | 200 updated TaskRead |\n| DELETE | `/tasks/{task_id}` | UUID path, no body | 204, empty body |\n| POST | `/events` | ONCE/WEEKLY example below | 201 EventRead |\n| GET | `/events` | `?limit=50&recurrence_type=WEEKLY` | 200 Page of EventRead (stored rules) |\n| GET | `/events/{event_id}` | UUID path, no body | 200 EventRead |\n| PATCH | `/events/{event_id}` | `{\"title\":\"Updated lecture\"}` | 200 updated EventRead |\n| DELETE | `/events/{event_id}` | UUID path, no body | 204, empty body; whole weekly rule |\n\n## Authentication example\n\n```json\n{\"email\":\"student@example.com\",\"password\":\"EXAMPLE_PASSWORD_REPLACE_ME\",\"full_name\":\"Student Name\"}\n```\n\nOnly register accepts full_name/username; login accepts email/password. Registration password is 8–1024 characters; login is 1–1024; email has basic format and max 320 validation, with final validation delegated to Supabase. Confirmation-required signup returns `session: null`; complete email confirmation then login. Profile metadata is validated and retained on first verified login. An already claimed optional username leaves the new profile username null; update it later through profile PATCH.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user\":{\"id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\"email\":\"student@example.com\"},\n  \"session\":{\"access_token\":\"ACCESS_TOKEN\",\"refresh_token\":\"REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"token_type\":\"bearer\",\"expires_in\":3600,\"expires_at\":1794823200},\n  \"confirmation_required\":false\n}\n```\n\nTokens here are placeholders. Keep them private. Replace the refresh token after each successful refresh; refresh can succeed while application DB is unavailable. Auth APIs and responses use Cache-Control: no-store. Invalid credentials use a generic 401; upstream details are not exposed. Authentication/provider rate limits return 429, with Retry-After when supplied. The backend intentionally leaves rate limiting to Supabase/provider and deployment ingress; it adds no distributed rate-limit store.\n\n## Profile and preferences examples\n\n```json\n{\"id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\"username\":null,\"full_name\":\"Student Name\",\"created_at\":\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\"}\n```\n\nUsername is optional, case-sensitive unique, max 100, and cannot be blank/padded. Full name is optional, max 200 and cannot be whitespace-only. Null clears either; owner/ID/timestamps cannot be edited.\n\nPreferences PATCH example:\n\n```json\n{\"timezone\":\"Africa/Cairo\",\"notifications_enabled\":true,\"preferred_work_start\":\"09:00:00\",\"preferred_work_end\":\"17:00:00\"}\n```\n\nPreferences response:\n\n```json\n{\"preference_id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\"user_id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\"timezone\":\"Africa/Cairo\",\"notifications_enabled\":true,\"preferred_work_start\":\"09:00:00\",\"preferred_work_end\":\"17:00:00\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\"}\n```\n\nTimezone must be supported IANA/UTC. Notifications is a JSON boolean. Work times use HH:MM:SS without offsets/fractions: both null or both non-null and unequal. Earlier end means overnight. PATCH validates combined old/new values, so clear both endpoints together.\n\n## Task example and validation\n\n```json\n{\"title\":\"Finish assignment\",\"task_type\":\"FLEXIBLE\",\"deadline\":\"2026-11-20T18:00:00+02:00\",\"estimated_duration_minutes\":60,\"category\":\"STUDY\",\"priority\":5,\"context\":\"Chapter 2\"}\n```\n\nTaskRead adds task_id, verified user_id, status UNSCHEDULED, created_at/updated_at, and null fixed endpoints for FLEXIBLE. Every GET/PATCH returns this same shape; lists wrap it in Page. Titles are nonblank/max 500; context nullable/max 500. Categories are STUDY, WORK, PERSONAL, HEALTH, MEETING. Duration is positive integer minutes; priority is integer 1–5 (5 highest), never a calculated score. Deadline is optional and may be in the past; any supplied timestamp needs an offset and is returned in UTC.\n\nFIXED also requires fixed_start_at and fixed_end_at, both offset-aware, end > start. FLEXIBLE requires both null. Switch FIXED to FLEXIBLE atomically:\n\n```json\n{\"task_type\":\"FLEXIBLE\",\"fixed_start_at\":null,\"fixed_end_at\":null}\n```\n\nLists additionally filter task_type, priority, deadline_from and deadline_to; deadline bounds are inclusive. Required fields cannot be explicitly null. Status/ID/owner/timestamps are output-only.\n\n## Event examples and validation\n\nONCE:\n\n```json\n{\"title\":\"Lecture\",\"category\":\"STUDY\",\"location\":\"Room 2\",\"start_at\":\"2026-11-16T09:00:00+02:00\",\"end_at\":\"2026-11-16T10:00:00+02:00\"}\n```\n\nWEEKLY overnight work/university timetable:\n\n```json\n{\"title\":\"Weekly shift\",\"category\":\"WORK\",\"recurrence_type\":\"WEEKLY\",\"recurrence_first_date\":\"2026-11-16\",\"recurrence_until_date\":\"2026-12-28\",\"recurrence_start_time\":\"22:00:00\",\"recurrence_end_time\":\"06:00:00\",\"recurrence_end_day_offset\":1,\"recurrence_timezone\":\"Africa/Cairo\",\"weekday\":1}\n```\n\nEventRead returns the submitted shape with event_id, verified user_id, source MANUAL, status SAVED, created_at/updated_at and every unused shape field null. Weekday is derived (ISO Monday=1..Sunday=7); optional input must match first date. ONCE requires timestamp endpoints and no weekly fields; WEEKLY requires local rule fields and no one-time endpoints. Until is optional and cannot precede first date. Offset 0 is same-day; 1 is next-day/overnight, including explicit 24-hour local intervals. Multi-weekday timetables use separate rules.\n\nFirst and bounded final endpoints reject DST ambiguity/nonexistence. The backend does not expand all intervening/future occurrences; consumers must resolve each interpreted endpoint in its timezone and validate positive UTC duration. Changing preferences timezone does not move an existing rule. PATCH changes the whole rule and must clear incompatible fields when switching recurrence type. A lecture/shift is an Event and never creates a duplicate Task.\n\n## Pagination and errors\n\n```json\n{\"items\":[],\"limit\":50,\"offset\":0,\"has_more\":false}\n```\n\nLimit 1–100, default 50; offset 0–1,000,000. Next offset is previous offset plus items.length. No COUNT query is used. Empty lists are 200. Task ordering is deadline/null-last then ID; event ordering uses relevant first/start date for recurrence-filtered lists, otherwise created_at then ID. No related profile/preferences collections are loaded.\n\nAll errors follow:\n\n```json\n{\"error\":{\"code\":\"invalid_request\",\"message\":\"Request validation failed\",\"details\":[{\"field\":\"body.priority\",\"message\":\"Input should be less than or equal to 5\"}]}}\n```\n\nPossible responses: 400 registration rejected; 401 missing/invalid/expired token or credentials; 404 missing/other-user resource; 409 uniqueness/profile conflict; 422 request or merged-record validation; 429 Auth rate limit; 502 Auth failure/invalid upstream session; 503 configuration/DB/Auth unavailable; 500 unexpected error. Invalid bearer responses include WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. Passwords, token values, raw request inputs, SQL and provider errors are excluded. Persisted text cannot contain U+0000.\n\n## Curl usage\n\n```powershell\ncurl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary '@login.json'\ncurl.exe http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/profiles/me -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN'\ncurl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/tasks -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary '@task.json'\ncurl.exe 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/events?recurrence_type=WEEKLY&limit=50' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN'\n```\n\nStore example request JSON in temporary local files, keep real passwords/tokens out of source control, and use Swagger's Authorize button for interactive tests. Business tables remain `public.profiles`, `user_preferences`, `tasks`, and `events`; Supabase owns `auth.users`. The initial migration and approved core model definitions are preserved.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Client[API client] --> API[FastAPI /api/v1 routers]\n    API --> JWT[Verified Supabase bearer identity]\n    JWT --> Session[Shared SQLAlchemy transaction]\n    Session --> RLS[PostgreSQL ownership / RLS]\n    RLS --> Tables[Profiles, preferences, tasks, events]\n    API --> Auth[Supabase Auth signup/login/refresh]\n    Modules[Registered teammate modules] --> API\n    Modules --> Base[Shared Base / metadata]\n    Base --> Alembic[One Alembic revision history]\n```\n\n## Responsibilities and file locations\n\n| File/package | Responsibility |\n|---|---|\n| `app/main.py` | Application factory, lifespan cleanup, health endpoints, API registration, security headers, optional CORS |\n| `app/config.py` | Central environment settings and endpoint/credential guards |\n| `app/auth.py` | Signature/issuer/audience/time/subject/role verification using trusted JWKS |\n| `app/dependencies.py` | Shared bearer dependency and function-scoped `SessionDep` |\n| `app/db/models.py` | Single shared Base and four approved core models; external Auth FK reference in separate metadata |\n| `app/db/session.py` | Shared runtime engine, role validation, transaction-local verified identity |\n| `app/db/registry.py` | Module model/router discovery and managed public-table allowlist |\n| `app/routers/` | REST endpoints and typed request/response contracts |\n| `app/services/` | Auth protocol, onboarding, preferences and owner-filtered persistence |\n| `app/schemas.py` | Validation, immutable input fields, response models and pagination |\n| `app/errors.py` / `app/openapi.py` | Error contract and usable API examples |\n| `alembic/` | One application migration environment and history |\n| `tests/` | Shared disposable database/identity fixtures and API/security tests |\n\n## Authentication and transactions\n\nPublic registration/login use the configured Supabase publishable/anon key. The backend forwards passwords only to the trusted Auth origin and never persists them. Confirmation-required signup returns no session and creates no profile. Verified login creates a missing profile and retains validated username/full_name metadata; existing profile changes are never overwritten. If a requested optional username is taken, onboarding leaves it null so login remains usable; profile PATCH can choose another name and still returns 409 on conflicts.\n\nRefresh verifies the returned JWT and subject and returns rotated tokens without requiring a database transaction. This prevents database downtime from discarding a newly rotated refresh token. Signup/login and application profile writes cannot be one distributed transaction; if database onboarding is unavailable after Auth succeeds, retry login when the database recovers. Do not create or delete an Auth account to compensate.\n\nProtected routes use `SessionDep`. A token is verified before connection acquisition. A dedicated runtime LOGIN must inherit authenticated, lack superuser/BYPASSRLS/administrative memberships, and have no ownership path to any registered application table. Per transaction, only verified subject/authenticated claims enter parameterized transaction-local settings. UTC and row_security are set locally too. Owner filters supplement PostgreSQL RLS; user_id never comes from the body.\n\nFunction-scoped dependency teardown commits or rolls back before the HTTP response is sent. Commit failures therefore cannot produce successful responses. Pool return rolls back residual transactions. Pool-size-one tests verify identity cleanup after success, failure, and connection reuse. Runtime credentials remain trusted backend secrets: SQL access with those credentials must never be given to end users.\n\nThe profile insert trigger creates exactly one preferences row. Existing triggers, column grants, CHECK constraints and policies remain active. IDs, owners, timestamps, task status and event source/status are read-only. No signup trigger is added to auth.users.\n\n## Configuration and lifecycle\n\n`Settings` reads `.env` without overriding injected environment values. Runtime uses only DATABASE_URL; Alembic/role provisioning use only MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL. Actual secrets, environments, local cluster files and signing keys are ignored. Remote database URLs require verify-full TLS; remote Auth requires HTTPS. Loopback HTTP Auth is permitted only in explicitly chosen development mode. Wildcard CORS is rejected; configure exact browser origins when necessary.\n\nNo network/SQL connection is made merely to import models or build OpenAPI. Engines and Auth HTTP connections are reused, with bounded pools and timeouts. Owned resources close in application lifespan cleanup. Missing Auth configuration allows local health/docs/test development but protected APIs remain unavailable until configured.\n\nJWT verification supports ES256/RS256 signing keys. HS256 is rejected; use asymmetric keys for local Supabase too. PyJWT 2.15.1+ supplies thread-safe JWKS caching, no redirects and a 30-second unknown-key refresh cooldown; the backend does not duplicate that cache. JWT NumericDate claims must be finite numbers (not booleans/strings), and the subject must be a non-nil UUID.\n\n## Validation and performance\n\nPATCH validates the merged record, not just submitted fields. Dates/instants remain finite; timestamps require offsets and normalize to UTC. Persisted strings reject whitespace-only required values and null characters. Collection limits are 1–100, default 50; offsets are 0–1,000,000. `has_more` uses limit+1 and avoids COUNT queries. List responses load no relationships, and query-count tests show no per-item queries. Existing owner/deadline and event owner/partial recurrence indexes support common filtering. Security role checks remain constant per transaction.\n\nWeekly rules retain local dates/times, end-day offset and their own timezone. ISO weekday derives from first_date. Validation resolves first and bounded final endpoints and rejects DST gaps/folds or non-positive resolved intervals. It cannot certify every intervening/future timezone transition. Any later consumer interpreting an occurrence must resolve both endpoints with `resolve_unambiguous_local_time` and check positive duration. No recurrence expansion API, occurrence rows, exceptions or optimizer is implemented.\n\n## Scope boundary\n\nTeammates add module packages and use the shared registry, session, Auth and migration history. No energy/attention calculations, Decision Engine, optimization, rescheduling, frontend code or frontend integration are included.\n"}}, "status": "completed", "stdout": "Success. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.\n# Escalation Requests\r\n\r\nCommands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:\r\n\r\n- Pipes: |\r\n- Logical operators: &&, ||\r\n- Command separators: ;\r\n- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)\r\n\r\nEach resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.\r\n\r\nExample:\r\n\r\ngit pull | tee output.txt\r\n\r\nThis is treated as two command segments:\r\n\r\n[\"git\", \"pull\"]\r\n\r\n[\"tee\", \"output.txt\"]\r\n\r\nCommands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.\r\n\r\n## How to request escalation\r\n\r\nIMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:\r\n\r\n- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `\"require_escalated\"`\r\n- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. \"Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?\"\r\n- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.\r\n\r\nIf you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with \"require_escalated\". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.\r\n\r\n## When to request escalation\r\n\r\nWhile commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:\r\n\r\n- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)\r\n- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.\r\n- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.\r\n- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.\r\n- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.\r\n\r\n## prefix_rule guidance\r\n\r\nWhen choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. This is a checklist you run yourself â€” not a subagent dispatch.\r\n\r\n**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.\r\n\r\n**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.\r\n\r\n**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.\r\n\r\n**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.\r\n\r\n**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.\r\n\r\nIf you find issues, fix them inline. login accepts email/password. Registration password is 8â€“1024 characters; login is 1â€“1024; email has basic format and max 320 validation, with final validation delegated to Supabase. Confirmation-required signup returns `session: null`; complete email confirmation then login. Profile metadata is validated and retained on first verified login. An already claimed optional username leaves the new profile username null; update it later through profile PATCH.\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"user\":{\"id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\"email\":\"student@example.com\"},\r\n  \"session\":{\"access_token\":\"ACCESS_TOKEN\",\"refresh_token\":\"REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"token_type\":\"bearer\",\"expires_in\":3600,\"expires_at\":1794823200},\r\n  \"confirmation_required\":false\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nTokens here are placeholders. Keep them private. Replace the refresh token after each successful refresh; refresh can succeed while application DB is unavailable. Auth APIs and responses use Cache-Control: no-store. Invalid credentials use a generic 401; upstream details are not exposed. Authentication/provider rate limits return 429, with Retry-After when supplied. The backend intentionally leaves rate limiting to Supabase/provider and deployment ingress; it adds no distributed rate-limit store.\r\n\r\n## Profile and preferences examples\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\"username\":null,\"full_name\":\"Student Name\",\"created_at\":\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\"}\r\n```\r\n\r\nUsername is optional, case-sensitive unique, max 100, and cannot be blank/padded. Full name is optional, max 200 and cannot be whitespace-only. Null clears either; owner/ID/timestamps cannot be edited.\r\n\r\nPreferences PATCH example:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"timezone\":\"Africa/Cairo\",\"notifications_enabled\":true,\"preferred_work_start\":\"09:00:00\",\"preferred_work_end\":\"17:00:00\"}\r\n```\r\n\r\nPreferences response:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"preference_id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\"user_id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\"timezone\":\"Africa/Cairo\",\"notifications_enabled\":true,\"preferred_work_start\":\"09:00:00\",\"preferred_work_end\":\"17:00:00\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\"}\r\n```\r\n\r\nTimezone must be supported IANA/UTC. Notifications is a JSON boolean. Work times use HH:MM:SS without offsets/fractions: both null or both non-null and unequal. Earlier end means overnight. PATCH validates combined old/new values, so clear both endpoints together.\r\n\r\n## Task example and validation\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"title\":\"Finish assignment\",\"task_type\":\"FLEXIBLE\",\"deadline\":\"2026-11-20T18:00:00+02:00\",\"estimated_duration_minutes\":60,\"category\":\"STUDY\",\"priority\":5,\"context\":\"Chapter 2\"}\r\n```\r\n\r\nTaskRead adds task_id, verified user_id, status UNSCHEDULED, created_at/updated_at, and null fixed endpoints for FLEXIBLE. Every GET/PATCH returns this same shape; lists wrap it in Page. Titles are nonblank/max 500; context nullable/max 500. Categories are STUDY, WORK, PERSONAL, HEALTH, MEETING. Duration is positive integer minutes; priority is integer 1â€“5 (5 highest), never a calculated score. Deadline is optional and may be in the past; any supplied timestamp needs an offset and is returned in UTC.\r\n\r\nFIXED also requires fixed_start_at and fixed_end_at, both offset-aware, end > start. FLEXIBLE requires both null. Switch FIXED to FLEXIBLE atomically:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"task_type\":\"FLEXIBLE\",\"fixed_start_at\":null,\"fixed_end_at\":null}\r\n```\r\n\r\nLists additionally filter task_type, priority, deadline_from and deadline_to; deadline bounds are inclusive. Required fields cannot be explicitly null. Status/ID/owner/timestamps are output-only.\r\n\r\n## Event examples and validation\r\n\r\nONCE:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"title\":\"Lecture\",\"category\":\"STUDY\",\"location\":\"Room 2\",\"start_at\":\"2026-11-16T09:00:00+02:00\",\"end_at\":\"2026-11-16T10:00:00+02:00\"}\r\n```\r\n\r\nWEEKLY overnight work/university timetable:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"title\":\"Weekly shift\",\"category\":\"WORK\",\"recurrence_type\":\"WEEKLY\",\"recurrence_first_date\":\"2026-11-16\",\"recurrence_until_date\":\"2026-12-28\",\"recurrence_start_time\":\"22:00:00\",\"recurrence_end_time\":\"06:00:00\",\"recurrence_end_day_offset\":1,\"recurrence_timezone\":\"Africa/Cairo\",\"weekday\":1}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEventRead returns the submitted shape with event_id, verified user_id, source MANUAL, status SAVED, created_at/updated_at and every unused shape field null. Weekday is derived (ISO Monday=1..Sunday=7); optional input must match first date. ONCE requires timestamp endpoints and no weekly fields; WEEKLY requires local rule fields and no one-time endpoints. Until is optional and cannot precede first date. Offset 0 is same-day; 1 is next-day/overnight, including explicit 24-hour local intervals. Multi-weekday timetables use separate rules.\r\n\r\nFirst and bounded final endpoints reject DST ambiguity/nonexistence. The backend does not expand all intervening/future occurrences; consumers must resolve each interpreted endpoint in its timezone and validate positive UTC duration. Changing preferences timezone does not move an existing rule. PATCH changes the whole rule and must clear incompatible fields when switching recurrence type. A lecture/shift is an Event and never creates a duplicate Task.\r\n\r\n## Pagination and errors\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"items\":[],\"limit\":50,\"offset\":0,\"has_more\":false}\r\n```\r\n\r\nLimit 1â€“100, default 50; offset 0â€“1,000,000. Next offset is previous offset plus items.length. No COUNT query is used. Empty lists are 200. Task ordering is deadline/null-last then ID; event ordering uses relevant first/start date for recurrence-filtered lists, otherwise created_at then ID. No related profile/preferences collections are loaded.\r\n\r\nAll errors follow:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"error\":{\"code\":\"invalid_request\",\"message\":\"Request validation failed\",\"details\":[{\"field\":\"body.priority\",\"message\":\"Input should be less than or equal to 5\"}]}}\r\n```\r\n\r\nPossible responses: 400 registration rejected; 401 missing/invalid/expired token or credentials; 404 missing/other-user resource; 409 uniqueness/profile conflict; 422 request or merged-record validation; 429 Auth rate limit; 502 Auth failure/invalid upstream session; 503 configuration/DB/Auth unavailable; 500 unexpected error. Invalid bearer responses include WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. Passwords, token values, raw request inputs, SQL and provider errors are excluded. Persisted text cannot contain U+0000.\r\n\r\n## Curl usage\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\ncurl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary '@login.json'\r\ncurl.exe http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/profiles/me -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN'\r\ncurl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/tasks -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary '@task.json'\r\ncurl.exe 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/events?recurrence_type=WEEKLY&limit=50' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN'\r\n```\r\n\r\nStore example request JSON in temporary local files, keep real passwords/tokens out of source control, and use Swagger's Authorize button for interactive tests. The backend APIs are ready for teammate integration; no client-side implementation is supplied.\r\n# Adding a backend module\r\n\r\nCreate only your module-owned files and tests. Reuse the shared foundation; never create another Base, engine, authentication system, Alembic environment, or users/tasks/events copy.\r\n\r\n## Exact files\r\n\r\n```text\r\napp/modules/<module>/\r\n  __init__.py       # empty package marker\r\n  models.py         # only module-owned models using shared Base\r\n  schemas.py        # Pydantic requests/responses, extra='forbid'\r\n  service.py        # ownership-filtered business queries\r\n  router.py         # APIRouter exported as router\r\ntests/test_<module>.py\r\nalembic/versions/<shared_revision>_<module>.py\r\n```\r\n\r\nDo not edit `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/auth.py`, `app/dependencies.py`, `app/db/session.py`, `app/db/models.py`, `app/db/registry.py`, `alembic.ini`, `alembic/env.py`, or the existing initial migration to register a module. Every registered module table requires non-null profile ownership. Migration review must add RLS and least-privilege column grants; the runtime guard rejects unmigrated tables, disabled RLS or accessible table ownership. Define useful owner-led indexes for actual queries. Never model auth.users on Base.\r\n\r\n## Router/session pattern\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter\r\nfrom app.dependencies import SessionDep\r\nfrom app.errors import ERROR_RESPONSES\r\n\r\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix='/your-module', tags=['Your module'],\r\n                   responses=ERROR_RESPONSES)\r\n\r\n@router.get('/records', response_model=YourResponse, summary='...',\r\n            description='Bearer token required; ...')\r\ndef endpoint(session: SessionDep):\r\n    user_id = session.info['user_id']  # verified subject\r\n    return service.list_owned(session, user_id=user_id)\r\n```\r\n\r\nDefine YourResponse and import your service in your own package. The application adds `/api/v1` automatically. Supply real request/response examples and error descriptions on your router. Do not manually commit, replace the identity, trust body user_id, or open a separate session inside a handler. Flush writes when needed; `SessionDep` handles final commit/rollback and cleanup before the response.\r\n\r\nEvery SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE includes the verified owner. IDs/defaults, owners and server-managed fields are excluded from writable grants. Ordinary queries use the separate restricted LOGIN, never table-owner/postgres/service-role credentials. Security-definer functions, if justified, require a fixed safe search_path, schema-qualified references, and tightly limited execution privileges.\r\n\r\n## Supabase deployment boundary\r\n\r\nNo remote Supabase connection or migration was performed. The registry permits only owned public application tables. Standard autogeneration does not fully inspect RLS, privileges, functions or triggers; review them separately.\\r\\n\\r\\n## RLS/grant pattern\\r\\n\\r\\nExample for a module-owned table with `id`, `user_id` and `title` (replace table names/columns with the reviewed module design):\\r\\n\\r\\n```sql\\r\\nALTER TABLE public.your_module_records ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\\r\\nREVOKE ALL ON public.your_module_records FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated;\\r\\nCREATE POLICY module_select_own ON public.your_module_records\\r\\n  FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (user_id = (SELECT auth.uid()));\\r\\nCREATE POLICY module_insert_own ON public.your_module_records\\r\\n  FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (user_id = (SELECT auth.uid()));\\r\\nCREATE POLICY module_update_own ON public.your_module_records\\r\\n  FOR UPDATE TO authenticated\\r\\n  USING (user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())) WITH CHECK (user_id = (SELECT auth.uid()));\\r\\nCREATE POLICY module_delete_own ON public.your_module_records\\r\\n  FOR DELETE TO authenticated USING (user_id = (SELECT auth.uid()));\\r\\nGRANT SELECT, DELETE ON public.your_module_records TO authenticated;\\r\\nGRANT INSERT (user_id, title) ON public.your_module_records TO authenticated;\\r\\nGRANT UPDATE (title) ON public.your_module_records TO authenticated;\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nNo anonymous access. IDs/defaults, owners and server-managed fields are excluded from writable grants. Ordinary queries use the separate restricted LOGIN, never table-owner/postgres/service-role credentials. Security-definer functions, if justified, require a fixed safe search_path, schema-qualified references, and tightly limited execution privileges.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Supabase deployment boundary\\r\\n\\r\\nNo remote Supabase connection or migration was performed. Remote DDL is blocked by default. Only after explicit approval and review, configure independent trusted migration/runtime URLs and use:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\n# Later only, after explicit approval:\\r\\n& '.\\\\.venv\\\\Scripts\\\\python.exe' -m alembic -x allow_remote_ddl=true upgrade head\\r\\n& '.\\\\.venv\\\\Scripts\\\\python.exe' -m scripts.provision_runtime --role scheduler_runtime --allow-remote\\r\\n& '.\\\\.venv\\\\Scripts\\\\python.exe' -m app.db.check\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nPrefer direct PostgreSQL or verified session-mode pooler port 5432, with verify-full TLS and trusted certificates. Transaction-pooler port 6543 is unsupported. Custom runtime-role support, migration/role-admin privileges, TLS and actual JWT signing configuration must be verified on the target project; never substitute a privileged runtime role to get around a failure. A connection check alone does not prove remote cross-user isolation.\\r\\n# Backend contribution workflow\\r\\n\\r\\nRead AGENTS.md at repository root and docs/backend-architecture.md. Changing preferences timezone does not move an existing rule. PATCH changes the whole rule and must clear incompatible fields when switching recurrence type. A lecture/shift is an Event and never creates a duplicate Task.\r\n\r\n## Pagination and errors\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\"items\":[],\"limit\":50,\"offset\":0,\"has_more\":false}\r\n```\r\n\r\nLimit 1â€“100, default 50; offset 0â€“1,000,000. whole weekly rule |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Authentication example\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"email\\\":\\\"student@example.com\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"EXAMPLE_PASSWORD_REPLACE_ME\\\",\\\"full_name\\\":\\\"Student Name\\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nOnly register accepts full_name/username; login accepts email/password. Registration password is 8â€“1024 characters; login is 1â€“1024; email has basic format and max 320 validation, with final validation delegated to Supabase. Confirmation-required signup returns `session: null`; complete email confirmation then login. Profile metadata is validated and retained on first verified login. An already claimed optional username leaves the new profile username null; update it later through profile PATCH.\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"user\\\":{\\\"id\\\":\\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\\\",\\\"email\\\":\\\"student@example.com\\\"},\\r\\n  \\\"session\\\":{\\\"access_token\\\":\\\"ACCESS_TOKEN\\\",\\\"refresh_token\\\":\\\"REFRESH_TOKEN\\\",\\\"token_type\\\":\\\"bearer\\\",\\\"expires_in\\\":3600,\\\"expires_at\\\":1794823200},\\r\\n  \\\"confirmation_required\\\":false\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nTokens here are placeholders. Keep them private. Replace the refresh token after each successful refresh; refresh can succeed while application DB is unavailable. Auth APIs and responses use Cache-Control: no-store. Invalid credentials use a generic 401; upstream details are not exposed. Authentication/provider rate limits return 429, with Retry-After when supplied. The backend intentionally leaves rate limiting to Supabase/provider and deployment ingress; it adds no distributed rate-limit store.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Profile and preferences examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"id\\\":\\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\\\",\\\"username\\\":null,\\\"full_name\\\":\\\"Student Name\\\",\\\"created_at\\\":\\\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\\\",\\\"updated_at\\\":\\\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUsername is optional, case-sensitive unique, max 100, and cannot be blank/padded. Full name is optional, max 200 and cannot be whitespace-only. Null clears either; owner/ID/timestamps cannot be edited.\\r\\n\\r\\nPreferences PATCH example:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"timezone\\\":\\\"Africa/Cairo\\\",\\\"notifications_enabled\\\":true,\\\"preferred_work_start\\\":\\\"09:00:00\\\",\\\"preferred_work_end\\\":\\\"17:00:00\\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nPreferences response:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"preference_id\\\":\\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\\\",\\\"user_id\\\":\\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\\\",\\\"timezone\\\":\\\"Africa/Cairo\\\",\\\"notifications_enabled\\\":true,\\\"preferred_work_start\\\":\\\"09:00:00\\\",\\\"preferred_work_end\\\":\\\"17:00:00\\\",\\\"updated_at\\\":\\\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nTimezone must be supported IANA/UTC. Notifications is a JSON boolean. Work times use HH:MM:SS without offsets/fractions: both null or both non-null and unequal. Earlier end means overnight. PATCH validates combined old/new values, so clear both endpoints together.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Task example and validation\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"title\\\":\\\"Finish assignment\\\",\\\"task_type\\\":\\\"FLEXIBLE\\\",\\\"deadline\\\":\\\"2026-11-20T18:00:00+02:00\\\",\\\"estimated_duration_minutes\\\":60,\\\"category\\\":\\\"STUDY\\\",\\\"priority\\\":5,\\\"context\\\":\\\"Chapter 2\\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nTaskRead adds task_id, verified user_id, status UNSCHEDULED, created_at/updated_at, and null fixed endpoints for FLEXIBLE. Every GET/PATCH returns this same shape; lists wrap it in Page. Titles are nonblank/max 500; context nullable/max 500. Categories are STUDY, WORK, PERSONAL, HEALTH, MEETING. Duration is positive integer minutes; priority is integer 1â€“5 (5 highest), never a calculated score. Deadline is optional and may be in the past; any supplied timestamp needs an offset and is returned in UTC.\\r\\n\\r\\nFIXED also requires fixed_start_at and fixed_end_at, both offset-aware, end > start. FLEXIBLE requires both null. Switch FIXED to FLEXIBLE atomically:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"task_type\\\":\\\"FLEXIBLE\\\",\\\"fixed_start_at\\\":null,\\\"fixed_end_at\\\":null}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nLists additionally filter task_type, priority, deadline_from and deadline_to; deadline bounds are inclusive. Required fields cannot be explicitly null. Status/ID/owner/timestamps are output-only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Event examples and validation\\r\\n\\r\\nONCE:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"title\\\":\\\"Lecture\\\",\\\"category\\\":\\\"STUDY\\\",\\\"location\\\":\\\"Room 2\\\",\\\"start_at\\\":\\\"2026-11-16T09:00:00+02:00\\\",\\\"end_at\\\":\\\"2026-11-16T10:00:00+02:00\\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWEEKLY overnight work/university timetable:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"title\\\":\\\"Weekly shift\\\",\\\"category\\\":\\\"WORK\\\",\\\"recurrence_type\\\":\\\"WEEKLY\\\",\\\"recurrence_first_date\\\":\\\"2026-11-16\\\",\\\"recurrence_until_date\\\":\\\"2026-12-28\\\",\\\"recurrence_start_time\\\":\\\"22:00:00\\\",\\\"recurrence_end_time\\\":\\\"06:00:00\\\",\\\"recurrence_end_day_offset\\\":1,\\\"recurrence_timezone\\\":\\\"Africa/Cairo\\\",\\\"weekday\\\":1}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nEventRead returns the submitted shape with event_id, verified user_id, source MANUAL, status SAVED, created_at/updated_at and every unused shape field null. Weekday is derived (ISO Monday=1..Sunday=7); optional input must match first date. ONCE requires timestamp endpoints and no weekly fields; WEEKLY requires local rule fields and no one-time endpoints. Until is optional and cannot precede first date. Offset 0 is same-day; 1 is next-day/overnight, including explicit 24-hour local intervals. Multi-weekday timetables use separate rules.\\r\\n\\r\\nFirst and bounded final endpoints reject DST ambiguity/nonexistence. The backend does not expand all intervening/future occurrences; consumers must resolve each interpreted endpoint in its timezone and validate positive UTC duration. Changing preferences timezone does not move an existing rule. PATCH changes the whole rule and must clear incompatible fields when switching recurrence type. A lecture/shift is an Event and never creates a duplicate Task.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Pagination and errors\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"items\\\":[],\\\"limit\\\":50,\\\"offset\\\":0,\\\"has_more\\\":false}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nLimit 1â€“100, default 50; offset 0â€“1,000,000. Next offset is previous offset plus items.length. No COUNT query is used. Empty lists are 200. Task ordering is deadline/null-last then ID; event ordering uses relevant first/start date for recurrence-filtered lists, otherwise created_at then ID. No related profile/preferences collections are loaded.\\r\\n\\r\\nAll errors follow:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\\"error\\\":{\\\"code\\\":\\\"invalid_request\\\",\\\"message\\\":\\\"Request validation failed\\\",\\\"details\\\":[{\\\"field\\\":\\\"body.priority\\\",\\\"message\\\":\\\"Input should be less than or equal to 5\\\"}]}}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible responses: 400 registration rejected; 401 missing/invalid/expired token or credentials; 404 missing/other-user resource; 409 uniqueness/profile conflict; 422 request or merged-record validation; 429 Auth rate limit; 502 Auth failure/invalid upstream session; 503 configuration/DB/Auth unavailable; 500 unexpected error. Invalid bearer responses include WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. Passwords, token values, raw request inputs, SQL and provider errors are excluded. Persisted text cannot contain U+0000.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Curl usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\ncurl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary '@login.json'\\r\\ncurl.exe http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/profiles/me -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN'\\r\\ncurl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/tasks -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary '@task.json'\\r\\ncurl.exe 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/events?recurrence_type=WEEKLY&limit=50' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ACCESS_TOKEN'\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nStore example request JSON in temporary local files, keep real passwords/tokens out of source control, and use Swagger's Authorize button for interactive tests. If the optional username is already claimed, onboarding can leave it null rather than blocking login.\\n+\\n+Failures: 422 for malformed email, password shorter than 8 or longer than 1024 characters, invalid profile text, or extra fields; 400 when Supabase rejects registration; 429 for provider rate limits; 502 for provider failure/unverifiable returned session; 503 for missing Auth configuration/provider connectivity or required database unavailability. Duplicate signup behavior depends on Supabase confirmation/privacy settings; do not assume every repeated signup returns 409.\\n+\\n+### B. `POST /api/v1/auth/login`\\n+\\n+Authentication: none. Login accepts only email/password, not registration profile fields. It provisions a missing own profile/default preferences after verification.\\n+\\n+Failures: 401 for incorrect credentials or an unconfirmed/rejected account; 422 for invalid email, empty password, password over 1024 characters, or extra fields; 429/502/503 for provider/configuration/dependency failures; 409 if onboarding cannot find the matching Auth user in the application database.\\n+\\n+Optional PowerShell login without displaying the password/token response:\\n+\\n+```powershell\\n+$manualBase = 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1'\\n+$manualEmail = Read-Host 'Your confirmed test account email'\\n+$manualSecret = Read-Host 'Test account password' -AsSecureString\\n+$manualPassword = [System.Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', $manualSecret).Password\\n+$manualLoginBody = @{ email = $manualEmail; password = $manualPassword } | ConvertTo-Json\\n+$manualLogin = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri \\\"$manualBase/auth/login\\\" `\\n+    -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $manualLoginBody\\n+$manualAccessToken = $manualLogin.session.access_token\\n+$manualRefreshToken = $manualLogin.session.refresh_token\\n+$manualHeaders = @{ Authorization = 'Bearer ' + $manualAccessToken }\\n+Remove-Variable manualPassword, manualLoginBody, manualSecret\\n+```\\n+\\n+### C. `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`\\n+\\n+Authentication: no bearer token required; provide the current refresh token. Run after successful login and replace the saved tokens before proceeding to CRUD.\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"refresh_token\\\": \\\"REPLACE_WITH_CURRENT_REFRESH_TOKEN\\\"\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+Expected success: **200**, the same `AuthResponse` shape as login, with a verified session and rotated token values. Save the newly returned access and refresh tokens. Refresh can succeed without application database availability; it does not perform database onboarding.\\n+\\n+Failures: 422 for an empty refresh token, over 4096 characters, or extra fields; 401 for a rejected/expired/revoked refresh token; 429 for rate limits; 502 for invalid provider response/unverifiable session; 503 for missing Auth configuration or unavailable provider. Configure authentication in Swagger\\n+\\n+1. Click **Authorize** near the top of Swagger.\\n+2. In the HTTP bearer input, paste only your actual access token. Do not include the word `Bearer`; Swagger adds it to the header.\\n+3. Click **Authorize**, then **Close**.\\n+4. Execute `GET /api/v1/profiles/me` to establish/retrieve your own profile before creating Tasks/Events.\\n+\\n+The HTTP header used by PowerShell or another client is:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_ACCESS_TOKEN\\n+```\\n+\\n+After refresh, replace the token in Swagger too. Profile and preferences\\n+\\n+Run these before scheduling inputs.
