Task CRUD\\n+\\n+Every Task endpoint requires a real bearer access token. First complete profile retrieval. Save the returned `task_id`; replace `{task_id}` with that actual UUID, without braces.\\n+\\n+### Request examples\\n+\\n+FLEXIBLE creation body:\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"title\\\": \\\"Manual A assignment\\\",\\n+  \\\"task_type\\\": \\\"FLEXIBLE\\\",\\n+  \\\"estimated_duration_minutes\\\": 60,\\n+  \\\"category\\\": \\\"STUDY\\\",\\n+  \\\"priority\\\": 5,\\n+  \\\"deadline\\\": \\\"2026-11-20T18:00:00+02:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"context\\\": \\\"Manual testing chapter\\\"\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+FIXED creation body for a second Task:\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"title\\\": \\\"Manual A fixed study session\\\",\\n+  \\\"task_type\\\": \\\"FIXED\\\",\\n+  \\\"estimated_duration_minutes\\\": 60,\\n+  \\\"category\\\": \\\"STUDY\\\",\\n+  \\\"priority\\\": 3,\\n+  \\\"fixed_start_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T09:00:00+02:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"fixed_end_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T10:00:00+02:00\\\"\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+Dates can be adjusted for your manual session; a past deadline is permitted by the implementation. Timestamps need UTC offsets and are returned in UTC. Categories are `STUDY`, `WORK`, `PERSONAL`, `HEALTH`, `MEETING`; importance is the integer field `priority`, 1-5. Estimated duration is a positive integer, at most 2147483647 minutes. FIXED endpoints must be present with end after start. FLEXIBLE endpoints must be null/omitted. Duration is not required to equal the fixed interval length.\\n+\\n+### Endpoint sequence\\n+\\n+| Order | Method/path | Example request body | Expected success | Expected failures |\\n+|---|---|---|---|---|\\n+| 1 | `POST /api/v1/tasks` | FLEXIBLE or FIXED body above | 201 complete `TaskRead` below | 422 invalid type/category/priority/duration/interval or forbidden fields; changed values and timestamps reflect your actual record. Status is always server-managed `UNSCHEDULED` in Sprint 1. Do not submit ID, owner, status, or timestamps.\\n+\\n+PATCH validates the combined stored/new record. For a FIXED Task, changing only its type to FLEXIBLE fails while stored fixed endpoints remain. This atomic switch succeeds:\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\\"task_type\\\":\\\"FLEXIBLE\\\",\\\"fixed_start_at\\\":null,\\\"fixed_end_at\\\":null}\\n+```\\n+\\n+Omitted fields stay unchanged; null clears nullable fields such as deadline/context. Required values cannot be set to null. After PATCH, GET the Task again. After final deletion, GET it again and expect 404.\\n+\\n+PowerShell creation example, using your existing `$manualHeaders`:\\n+\\n+```powershell\\n+$manualTaskBody = @{\\n+    title = 'Manual A assignment'\\n+    task_type = 'FLEXIBLE'\\n+    estimated_duration_minutes = 60\\n+    category = 'STUDY'\\n+    priority = 5\\n+} | ConvertTo-Json\\n+$manualTask = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri \\\"$manualBase/tasks\\\" `\\n+    -Headers $manualHeaders -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $manualTaskBody\\n+$manualTaskId = $manualTask.task_id\\n+Invoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri \\\"$manualBase/tasks/$manualTaskId\\\" -Headers $manualHeaders\\n+```\\n+\\n+## 10. Event CRUD: ONCE and WEEKLY\\n+\\n+Every Event endpoint requires a real bearer access token. Lectures/work shifts are Events and do not create duplicate Tasks. Save each returned `event_id`; use actual UUIDs in path inputs.\\n+\\n+### ONCE creation body\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"title\\\": \\\"Manual A lecture\\\",\\n+  \\\"category\\\": \\\"STUDY\\\",\\n+  \\\"location\\\": \\\"Room 2\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_type\\\": \\\"ONCE\\\",\\n+  \\\"start_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T09:00:00+02:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"end_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T10:00:00+02:00\\\"\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+ONCE is the default if recurrence_type is omitted. End must follow start, timestamps need offsets, and weekly fields must be null/omitted.\\n+\\n+### WEEKLY timetable creation body\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"title\\\": \\\"Manual A weekly work shift\\\",\\n+  \\\"category\\\": \\\"WORK\\\",\\n+  \\\"location\\\": \\\"Office\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_type\\\": \\\"WEEKLY\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_first_date\\\": \\\"2026-11-16\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_until_date\\\": \\\"2026-12-28\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_start_time\\\": \\\"22:00:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_end_time\\\": \\\"06:00:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_end_day_offset\\\": 1,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_timezone\\\": \\\"Africa/Cairo\\\",\\n+  \\\"weekday\\\": 1\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+November 16, 2026 is Monday, ISO weekday 1. If you change the first date, update weekday to match or omit weekday and let the backend derive it. ISO weekdays run Monday=1 through Sunday=7. For a lecture on Monday and Wednesday, create two separate weekly rules.\\n+\\n+WEEKLY requires first date, local whole-second start/end times, end-day offset, and timezone. Until is optional but cannot precede first date. Use offset 0 for a same-day interval with end later than start; offset 1 supports overnight intervals. ONCE endpoints must be null/omitted. Changing preferences timezone does not change a rule's stored timezone.\\n+\\n+### Endpoint sequence\\n+\\n+| Order | Method/path | Example request body | Expected success | Expected failures |\\n+|---|---|---|---|---|\\n+| 1 | `POST /api/v1/events` | ONCE body above | 201 complete ONCE `EventRead` below | 422 invalid interval/category/shape or forbidden fields; 409 missing profile; 401/503 authentication/dependency errors |\\n+| 2 | `POST /api/v1/events` | WEEKLY body above | 201 complete WEEKLY `EventRead` below | 422 missing rule fields, invalid dates/weekday/timezone/DST endpoints or mixed shapes; 409/401/503 as above |\\n+| 3 | `GET /api/v1/events/{event_id}` | None | 200 complete stored `EventRead` | 404 missing/other-user ID; 422 malformed UUID; 401/503 |\\n+| 4 | `GET /api/v1/events` | None; query example `?limit=2&recurrence_type=WEEKLY` | 200 page of complete `EventRead` objects | 422 invalid pagination/category/recurrence query values; 401/503 |\\n+| 5 | `PATCH /api/v1/events/{event_id}` | `{\\\"title\\\":\\\"Manual A lecture updated\\\",\\\"location\\\":\\\"Room 3\\\"}` | 200 complete updated `EventRead` | 404 missing/other-user ID; 422 invalid merged rule/interval/UUID/forbidden fields; 401/503 |\\n+| Final cleanup | `DELETE /api/v1/events/{event_id}` | None | 204, empty body; entire stored rule if WEEKLY | 404 missing/other-user/already deleted ID; 422 malformed UUID; 401/503 |\\n+\\n+Example ONCE `EventRead`:\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"title\\\": \\\"Manual A lecture\\\",\\n+  \\\"category\\\": \\\"STUDY\\\",\\n+  \\\"location\\\": \\\"Room 2\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_type\\\": \\\"ONCE\\\",\\n+  \\\"start_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T07:00:00Z\\\",\\n+  \\\"end_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_first_date\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_until_date\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_start_time\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_end_time\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_end_day_offset\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_timezone\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"event_id\\\": \\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003\\\",\\n+  \\\"user_id\\\": \\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\\\",\\n+  \\\"source\\\": \\\"MANUAL\\\",\\n+  \\\"status\\\": \\\"SAVED\\\",\\n+  \\\"created_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\\\",\\n+  \\\"updated_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\\\",\\n+  \\\"weekday\\\": null\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+Example WEEKLY `EventRead`:\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"title\\\": \\\"Manual A weekly work shift\\\",\\n+  \\\"category\\\": \\\"WORK\\\",\\n+  \\\"location\\\": \\\"Office\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_type\\\": \\\"WEEKLY\\\",\\n+  \\\"start_at\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"end_at\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_first_date\\\": \\\"2026-11-16\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_until_date\\\": \\\"2026-12-28\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_start_time\\\": \\\"22:00:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_end_time\\\": \\\"06:00:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_end_day_offset\\\": 1,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_timezone\\\": \\\"Africa/Cairo\\\",\\n+  \\\"event_id\\\": \\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005\\\",\\n+  \\\"user_id\\\": \\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\\\",\\n+  \\\"source\\\": \\\"MANUAL\\\",\\n+  \\\"status\\\": \\\"SAVED\\\",\\n+  \\\"created_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\\\",\\n+  \\\"updated_at\\\": \\\"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\\\",\\n+  \\\"weekday\\\": 1\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+GET/PATCH return these same complete shapes, with actual IDs/values/timestamps. Source/status stay server-managed MANUAL/SAVED. No generated occurrences or exception records are returned.\\n+\\n+PATCH applies to the entire weekly rule. Changing only the type while keeping incompatible stored fields fails. Example conversion of an existing ONCE Event to WEEKLY:\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"recurrence_type\\\": \\\"WEEKLY\\\",\\n+  \\\"start_at\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"end_at\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_first_date\\\": \\\"2026-11-16\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_start_time\\\": \\\"09:00:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_end_time\\\": \\\"10:00:00\\\",\\n+  \\\"recurrence_end_day_offset\\\": 0,\\n+  \\\"recurrence_timezone\\\": \\\"Africa/Cairo\\\",\\n+  \\\"weekday\\\": 1\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+To convert WEEKLY to ONCE, provide valid start_at/end_at and set all weekly rule fields, including weekday, to null in the same PATCH. After every PATCH, GET the record. After final deletion, GET it and expect 404.\\n+\\n+## 11. Pagination and filtering\\n+\\n+Requires a real bearer token and manually created records. Create at least three matching Tasks and three matching Events before checking multiple pages. Keep records unchanged while comparing pages.\\n+\\n+Both list endpoints return this page structure; this is an exact empty-page example:\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\\"items\\\":[],\\\"limit\\\":2,\\\"offset\\\":0,\\\"has_more\\\":false}\\n+```\\n+\\n+For non-empty pages, `items` contains full TaskRead or EventRead objects shown above. There is no total/count field. Default limit is 50; allowed limit is 1-100 and offset 0-1000000. `has_more` indicates whether another item exists after this page. For the next page, increase offset by the number of returned items.\\n+\\n+| Method/path example | Authentication/body | Expected result/failure |\\n+|---|---|---|\\n+| `GET /api/v1/tasks?limit=2&offset=0` | Bearer; no body | 200, at most two own Tasks; has_more true if more matching records exist |\\n+| `GET /api/v1/tasks?limit=2&offset=2` | Bearer; no body | 200 next page; no overlap while data remains unchanged |\\n+| `GET /api/v1/tasks?category=STUDY&task_type=FLEXIBLE&priority=5` | Bearer; no body | 200 own Tasks matching all filters |\\n+| `GET /api/v1/tasks?deadline_from=2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&deadline_to=2026-11-21T23:59:59Z` | Bearer; no body | 200 matching Tasks; deadline boundaries are inclusive and exclude null deadlines |\\n+| `GET /api/v1/events?limit=2&offset=0&category=WORK&recurrence_type=WEEKLY` | Bearer; no body | 200 matching own stored rules; one record per rule, not per occurrence |\\n+| `GET /api/v1/events?recurrence_type=ONCE` | Bearer; no body | 200 own ONCE Events only |\\n+\\n+Task ordering is deadline ascending, null last, then task_id. ONCE-filtered Event ordering is start_at/event_id; WEEKLY-filtered ordering is recurrence_first_date/event_id; unfiltered Event ordering is created_at/event_id. An empty result is 200, not 404.\\n+\\n+Invalid pagination/category/type/priority/deadline inputs return 422; missing/invalid authentication returns 401; unavailable dependencies can return 503. Query priority is a number 1-5. Use UTC `Z` in URL timestamps, or URL-encode a plus offset as `%2B`; Swagger handles query encoding.\\n+\\n+PowerShell list example:\\n+\\n+```powershell\\n+Invoke-RestMethod -Method Get `\\n+    -Uri \\\"$manualBase/tasks?limit=2&offset=0&category=STUDY\\\" -Headers $manualHeaders\\n+```\\n+\\n+## 12. Invalid inputs and expected errors\\n+\\n+Change one input at a time. Confirm failures leave the existing record unchanged by GETting it again. Do not deliberately interrupt databases, corrupt tokens, or flood the provider to manufacture infrastructure failures.\\n+\\n+### Checks possible without real Supabase credentials\\n+\\n+| Request/action | Expected result |\\n+|---|---|\\n+| Swagger Logout, then `GET /api/v1/profiles/me`, `/preferences/me`, `/tasks`, or `/events` | 401 and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` |\\n+| `POST /api/v1/auth/register` with `{\\\"email\\\":\\\"bad\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"short\\\"}` | 422 schema validation before contacting Auth |\\n+| `POST /api/v1/auth/login` with `{\\\"email\\\":\\\"bad\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"\\\"}` | 422 schema validation before contacting Auth |\\n+| `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` with `{\\\"refresh_token\\\":\\\"\\\"}` | 422 schema validation before contacting Auth |\\n+\\n+Protected validation checks below should use a valid real token; without it, authentication/dependency errors can happen before field validation.\\n+\\n+### Authenticated input checks\\n+\\n+| Endpoint/action | Invalid example | Expected result |\\n+|---|---|---|\\n+| `PATCH /profiles/me` | `{\\\"id\\\":\\\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006\\\"}` | 422 forbidden field |\\n+| `PATCH /profiles/me` | `{\\\"full_name\\\":\\\"   \\\"}` or `{\\\"username\\\":\\\" padded \\\"}` | 422 |\\n+| `PATCH /profiles/me` | A username already owned by the other manual account | 409; previous profile remains unchanged |\\n+| `PATCH /preferences/me` | `{\\\"timezone\\\":\\\"Invalid/Zone\\\"}` or `{\\\"notifications_enabled\\\":\\\"yes\\\"}` | 422 |\\n+| `PATCH /preferences/me` | Clear only one endpoint of a stored non-null work window | 422 merged interval validation |\\n+| `POST /tasks` | Valid Task body changed to priority 0/6, duration 0, category OTHER, or title whitespace-only | 422 |\\n+| `POST /tasks` | Add `\\\"user_id\\\"`, `\\\"status\\\"`, generated ID, or timestamps to a valid body | 422 |\\n+| `POST /tasks` | FIXED without both endpoints; or FLEXIBLE with a fixed endpoint | 422 |\\n+| `PATCH /tasks/{task_id}` | `{\\\"priority\\\":null}` | 422 required value cannot be null |\\n+| `POST /events` | ONCE end equal to/before start, or timestamps without offsets | 422 |\\n+| `POST /events` | WEEKLY until before first date; weekday not matching first date; missing timezone; negative day offset | 422 |\\n+| `POST /events` | Mix ONCE start_at/end_at with weekly fields | 422 |\\n+| `PATCH /events/{event_id}` | Add source/status/user_id, or leave an invalid combined interval | 422 |\\n+| Task/Event GET/PATCH/DELETE by ID | `not-a-uuid` as path input | 422 with a valid token |\\n+| Task/Event GET/PATCH/DELETE by ID | Well-formed UUID that does not exist, with an otherwise valid body where needed | 404 |\\n+| Either collection GET | limit=0/101, offset=-1/1000001, category=OTHER | 422 |\\n+| Task collection GET | Upper deadline bound earlier than lower bound | 422 |\\n+\\n+Path prefixes in this table are `/api/v1`.\\n+\\n+For a manual DST rejection check, use a valid WEEKLY body with recurrence_timezone `America/New_York`, first date `2026-03-08`, weekday 7, start `02:30:00`, end `03:30:00`, and end-day offset 0; omit until. Expected 422 because the first start falls in the spring DST gap. An analogous first-date fold example is `2026-11-01`, weekday 7, start `01:30:00`, end `02:30:00`, offset 0: expected 422 for ambiguity.\\n+\\n+Weekly validation checks first and bounded final occurrence endpoints. It does not certify every intervening/future DST transition or expand occurrences. Later scheduling consumers must resolve each interpreted occurrence themselves.\\n+\\n+Example validation error shape:\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"error\\\": {\\n+    \\\"code\\\": \\\"invalid_request\\\",\\n+    \\\"message\\\": \\\"Request validation failed\\\",\\n+    \\\"details\\\": [\\n+      {\\n+        \\\"field\\\": \\\"body.priority\\\",\\n+        \\\"message\\\": \\\"Input should be less than or equal to 5\\\"\\n+      }\\n+    ]\\n+  }\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+All backend errors use `error.code`, `error.message`, and `error.details` (an array, sometimes empty). Exact validation messages/field locations depend on the rejected rule. Other useful statuses:\\n+\\n+- 400: registration rejected by Auth.\\n+- 401: invalid/missing/expired bearer token, or rejected login/refresh credentials.\\n+- 404: absent or other-user Task/Event.\\n+- 409: uniqueness or profile/Auth-user dependency conflict.\\n+- 422: request or combined-record validation.\\n+- 429: Auth rate limit; honor Retry-After if present.\\n+- 502: failed/invalid/unverifiable Auth provider response.\\n+- 503: configuration, restricted runtime role, database, or Auth availability issue.\\n+- 500: unexpected backend error; record the route/status and sanitized response for investigation.\\n+\\n+Invalid bearer checks require working verifier configuration to establish a meaningful 401. With an incompatible signing algorithm, login can return 502 for an unverifiable upstream session, while protected requests reject its token with 401. Do not change security rules to make that token work.\\n+\\n+## 13. Verify two-user isolation\\n+\\n+This requires two real accounts in the same configured Supabase project. Do not use administrator/service-role tokens for either account.\\n+\\n+1. With User A authorized, create at least one Task and one Event. Save their IDs and A's profile ID. Set a recognizable profile name/preferences value.\\n+2. Register/confirm/login User B. Log out A in Swagger and authorize using B's access token, or use separate normal/private browser sessions. Maintain separate PowerShell token/header variables if using PowerShell.\\n+3. As B, list Tasks/Events: A's saved IDs must not appear.\\n+4. As B, GET A's Task/Event by ID: expect 404.\\n+5. As B, PATCH A's Task/Event using a valid body such as `{\\\"title\\\":\\\"Manual cross-user attempt\\\"}`: expect 404.\\n+6. As B, DELETE A's Task/Event: expect 404.\\n+7. As B, GET `/profiles/me` and `/preferences/me`: IDs must identify B, not A. PATCH B's profile/preferences and then switch back to A; A's values must remain unchanged.\\n+8. As B, supplying A's ID/user_id in profile/preferences/Task/Event request bodies must return 422. Ownership is derived from the token.\\n+9. Reauthorize A. GET A's saved Task/Event and check they still exist and have their original values. Repeat the resource checks in reverse using B's records.\\n+\\n+There are no `/profiles/{user_id}` or `/preferences/{user_id}` endpoints. A 404 from an invented route does not prove ownership enforcement; use the actual `/me` APIs and cross-user body rejection checks.\\n+\\n+Record only status codes and non-secret IDs/titles for your comparison. A dependency error such as 503 is not evidence of isolation. Dashboard/administrator table access is not an end-user RLS test.\\n+\\n+## 14. Inspect persisted data safely\\n+\\n+Start with authenticated GET requests: after POST/PATCH, repeat GET by ID and collection GET. Reload Swagger and repeat GET to confirm the record is stored rather than just displayed in an earlier response. A frontend cache is not involved.\\n+\\n+Optional SQL inspection is for a trusted local database operator using an existing authorized inspection connection. Do not create roles, disable RLS, alter tables, or query Auth passwords/tokens. Inspect only your manual records with SELECTs and bounded results.\\n+\\n+If using the portable local PostgreSQL binaries, open psql with your actual local inspection username/database/port. `-W` prompts for the password without putting it in command arguments:\\n+\\n+```powershell\\n+& '.\\\\.local\\\\pgsql\\\\bin\\\\psql.exe' -h 127.0.0.1 -p 55432 `\\n+    -U REPLACE_LOCAL_INSPECTION_USERNAME -d REPLACE_LOCAL_DB_NAME -W\\n+```\\n+\\n+Alternatively, use your existing local pgAdmin connection. Replace the example UUID below with your actual profile `id`, then run a read-only transaction:\\n+\\n+```sql\\n+BEGIN READ ONLY;\\n+\\n+SELECT id, username, full_name, created_at, updated_at\\n+FROM public.profiles\\n+WHERE id = '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'::uuid;\\n+\\n+SELECT preference_id, user_id, timezone, notifications_enabled,\\n+       preferred_work_start, preferred_work_end, updated_at\\n+FROM public.user_preferences\\n+WHERE user_id = '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'::uuid;\\n+\\n+SELECT task_id, user_id, title, task_type, priority, status,\\n+       estimated_duration_minutes, deadline, fixed_start_at, fixed_end_at\\n+FROM public.tasks\\n+WHERE user_id = '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'::uuid\\n+ORDER BY created_at DESC, task_id\\n+LIMIT 20;\\n+\\n+SELECT event_id, user_id, title, recurrence_type, start_at, end_at,\\n+       recurrence_first_date, recurrence_until_date,\\n+       recurrence_start_time, recurrence_end_time,\\n+       recurrence_end_day_offset, recurrence_timezone, source, status\\n+FROM public.events\\n+WHERE user_id = '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'::uuid\\n+ORDER BY created_at DESC, event_id\\n+LIMIT 20;\\n+\\n+COMMIT;\\n+```\\n+\\n+An unscoped restricted runtime SQL connection can return no owned rows because `auth.uid()` is null; that is expected. Do not forge SQL identity claims or use a privileged role as the API runtime. Use the authenticated API to inspect your user's rows. A trusted administrator inspection connection may see records independently of RLS, so it demonstrates persistence only, not authorization.\\n+\\n+For an already prepared hosted test project, you can personally inspect the four public application tables in the Supabase dashboard **Table Editor**, filtering by your manual user/record IDs. Do not edit/delete existing records there. The WEEKLY `weekday` response field is derived from recurrence_first_date; it is not a stored database column.\\n+\\n+For cleanup, return to Swagger as the owning user and DELETE only the Task/Event IDs you created during this session. Expect 204, then 404 when GETting them. Do not delete profiles/Auth users/preferences or reset/drop databases as part of this guide.\\n+\\n+## 15. Stop the server and clear the manual session\\n+\\n+In the terminal running Uvicorn, press **Ctrl+C**. Expected output includes application shutdown/server process finished. This stops FastAPI and closes its connections; it does not delete database data. Leave an existing/shared PostgreSQL server running.\\n+\\n+Log out Swagger authorization and close the browser session. Close the second PowerShell terminal containing token variables, or remove those variables when finished. Exit psql with `\\\\q`. Do not save session responses containing tokens into tracked files.\\n+\\n+## 16. Supabase dashboard details for a later approved setup\\n+\\n+Database deployment and Auth configuration are separate from manual testing. Prerequisites and testing order\n\nYou need Windows PowerShell, a browser, Python 3.12 or newer, the backend dependencies, and an existing configured database. The current workspace already has a virtual environment and local PostgreSQL setup. Reuse them; do not initialize/reset a database or reapply migrations for this guide.\n\nThere are two distinct testing environments:\n\n| Environment | What you can do | What it requires |\n|---|---|---|\n| Native local PostgreSQL, without real Supabase Auth | Start FastAPI; open Swagger/OpenAPI; use public health endpoints; check missing-token errors and schema-only validation errors | Existing local database/schema and restricted runtime credentials; no Supabase token |\n| Backend with real Supabase Auth | Successful registration/login/refresh, profiles/preferences, Task/Event CRUD, filtering and two-user isolation | Configured local Supabase stack or an explicitly chosen non-production Supabase project; application schema and runtime role already prepared in that same database |\n\nThe native local database's minimal Auth fixture is not a real login service. A hosted Supabase token alone does not make that local database ready for authenticated CRUD: its `auth.users` identities must match the Auth service. Do not manually copy Auth users or create another users table. Use a matched local Supabase Auth/database stack or the same hosted project's Auth/database for real-user testing.\n\nRecommended order:\n\n1. Prepare the environment and check local connectivity.\n2. Start FastAPI, open Swagger, and check health.\n3. Register/confirm/login User A, then refresh its session.\n4. Authorize Swagger; retrieve/update A's profile and preferences.\n5. Create/read/list/update Tasks, keeping their IDs.\n6. Create/read/list/update ONCE and WEEKLY Events, keeping their IDs.\n7. Test pagination, filters, and invalid inputs.\n8. Register/login User B and check isolation in both directions.\n9. Inspect persistence; then delete only records you created for this manual session.\n10. Stop FastAPI.\n\nUse distinctive titles such as `Manual A assignment` and `Manual A lecture`. Keep manual test data separate from existing data. A DELETE endpoint permanently deletes its target, so leave deletion until the final cleanup step.\n\n## 2. PowerShell environment setup\n\nFrom the repository root:\n\n```powershell\nSet-Location -LiteralPath 'code/backend'\n```\n\nOn a fresh machine only, if the virtual environment/dependencies are absent:\n\n```powershell\npy -3 -m venv .venv\n& '.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe' -m pip install -r requirements.lock\n```\n\nAn existing `.env` must be preserved. If it is absent, copy `.env.example` once and fill in private values locally:\n\n```powershell\nif (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath '.env')) {\n    Copy-Item -LiteralPath '.env.example' -Destination '.env'\n}\n```\n\nConfiguration responsibilities:\n\n| Variable | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `APP_ENV` | `development` for local work. Only explicit development permits loopback HTTP Supabase Auth. |\n| `DATABASE_URL` | Existing restricted PostgreSQL runtime LOGIN; never postgres/table-owner/service-role credentials for CRUD. |\n| `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` | Separate migration/admin connection. Not used for these manual API requests. |\n| `SUPABASE_URL` | Trusted Auth project origin, such as `https://REPLACE_PROJECT_REF.supabase.co`; local Supabase uses its actual loopback origin. |\n| `SUPABASE_PUBLIC_KEY` | The same project's publishable key or legacy anon key. |\n| `SUPABASE_JWT_AUDIENCE` | `authenticated`. |\n| `CORS_ORIGINS` | Optional exact browser origins; Swagger served by this backend does not need a separate frontend origin. |\n| `BACKEND_MODULES` | Existing optional module registration; leave its current value alone. |\n\nThe backend loads `code/backend/.env`. Already set process environment variables override `.env`, so use the same environment in each relevant terminal and restart FastAPI after changing configuration. Do not print the complete environment or `.env` into a transcript.\n\nFor native local health/docs use without Auth, the Auth variables can remain unset; do not leave fake credential values in them. Successful authenticated operations require real configuration. No authentication bypass is available.\n\nA local runtime URL has this form; use your existing actual database name, port, and restricted role:\n\n```dotenv\nAPP_ENV=development\nDATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://REPLACE_RESTRICTED_ROLE:URL_ENCODED_PRIVATE_PASSWORD@127.0.0.1:55432/REPLACE_LOCAL_DB_NAME\n```\n\nFor remote PostgreSQL, the implementation requires `sslmode=verify-full` and a trusted certificate configuration. It rejects transaction-pooler port 6543; use direct or verified session-mode connectivity on port 5432. Configuration is explained further in the [backend README](../code/backend/README.md). If schema/runtime-role preparation is missing, pause authenticated testing and arrange that setup separately; this guide contains no schema-changing commands.\n\n## 3. Check the existing local database\n\nBefore running the following yourself, privately confirm `DATABASE_URL` targets `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, or `::1`. This section is for the existing local database, not a hosted Supabase connection.\n\n```powershell\n& '.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe' -m app.db.check\n```\n\nExpected successful output:\n\n```text\nConnection OK; restricted role and RLS prerequisites verified; no scoped user identity.\n```\n\nThis checks runtime connectivity/role prerequisites; it does not prove two-user isolation. Failure can mean the server is stopped, connection details are wrong, the application schema is absent, or the runtime role is unsafe. Do not replace restricted credentials with admin credentials to get a pass.\n\nIf using the existing portable local PostgreSQL installation:\n\n```powershell\n& '.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe' -m scripts.local_postgres status\n# Only if the existing server is stopped:\n& '.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe' -m scripts.local_postgres start\n```\n\nIf the script fails but the connectivity command succeeds, the database is reachable. Do not initialize another cluster or reset the current one.\n\n## 4. Start FastAPI and open Swagger\n\nIn the backend PowerShell terminal:\n\n```powershell\n& '.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe' -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000\n```\n\nLeave that terminal open. Expected startup includes `Application startup complete` and the listening address. If port 8000 is occupied, choose another unused port and substitute it throughout the guide.\n\nOpen these addresses in your browser:\n\n- Swagger UI: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`\n- ReDoc: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/redoc`\n- OpenAPI JSON: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/openapi.json`\n\nIn Swagger, expand an operation, click **Try it out**, replace the example/query/path values, then click **Execute**. Read the **Server response** status/body. The displayed documented response examples are not execution results.\n\nAll endpoint paths below include `/api/v1`.\n\n### Public health endpoints: no Supabase token needed\n\n| Order | Method/path | Authentication | Request body | Expected success | Expected failures |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| First | `GET /api/v1/health` | None | None | 200, `{\"status\":\"ok\"}` | Connection refused if FastAPI is not running; unexpected server failure 500 |\n| Second | `GET /api/v1/health/ready` | None | None | 200, `{\"status\":\"ready\"}` | 503 for unavailable/misconfigured database or unsafe runtime role |\n\nIn a second PowerShell terminal:\n\n```powershell\n$manualBase = 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1'\nInvoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri \"$manualBase/health\"\nInvoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri \"$manualBase/health/ready\"\n```\n\nLiveness can succeed while readiness fails. Successful readiness does not establish Auth configuration or user isolation.\n\n## 5. Obtain a real Supabase access token yourself\n\nUse a test account in your chosen local/non-production Supabase environment. You cannot use a project API key, database password, dashboard login, user UUID, or refresh token as an access token.\n\nPreferred flow:\n\n1. Configure the matching `SUPABASE_URL`, public key, and database privately.\n2. Check in the Supabase dashboard that the Email provider/password login is enabled. Dashboard labels vary; look under **Authentication** for providers/sign-in settings.\n3. Use `POST /api/v1/auth/register` below with an email address you control.\n4. If `confirmation_required` is true, follow the confirmation email before logging in. For local Supabase, use the local mail interface reported by its existing setup.\n5. Call `POST /api/v1/auth/login`.\n6. Copy `session.access_token` from the successful backend response privately. Keep `session.refresh_token` for the refresh test.\n\nThe dashboard's **Authentication → Users** view can show that your account exists; it does not provide that user's current login session/access token.\n\nAlternative if backend login is blocked by application database setup: obtain a token directly from Supabase Auth yourself, using the same project's public key and your test-account email/password. This is an Auth HTTP request, not a backend endpoint, and its response uses Supabase's own top-level token fields:\n\n```powershell\n$manualSupabaseUrl = Read-Host 'Supabase project origin, without /auth/v1'\n$manualPublicKey = Read-Host 'Publishable or anon key'\n$manualEmail = Read-Host 'Your confirmed test account email'\n$manualSecret = Read-Host 'Test account password' -AsSecureString\n$manualPassword = [System.Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', $manualSecret).Password\n$manualAuthBody = @{ email = $manualEmail; password = $manualPassword } | ConvertTo-Json\n$manualDirectSession = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post `\n    -Uri \"$($manualSupabaseUrl.TrimEnd('/'))/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password\" `\n    -Headers @{ apikey = $manualPublicKey } `\n    -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $manualAuthBody\n$manualAccessToken = $manualDirectSession.access_token\n$manualRefreshToken = $manualDirectSession.refresh_token\nRemove-Variable manualPassword, manualAuthBody, manualSecret\n```\n\nDo not print `$manualDirectSession`, record the command in a transcript, or save tokens in tracked files. Invalid credentials/unconfirmed accounts are rejected by Supabase. Obtaining a token this way does not repair a missing application schema/runtime role or mismatched database.\n\nThe existing backend accepts **ES256/RS256** access-token signing and verifies the trusted project's JWKS, issuer, audience, role, expiration, and user UUID. It rejects legacy HS256 tokens. Check the active signing algorithm in **Authentication → JWT Signing Keys** or the corresponding signing-key settings. An incompatible signing setup needs a separate planned configuration change; do not share the JWT secret/private key or generate a substitute token.\n\n## 6. Registration, login, and refresh\n\nThese routes require a real configured Supabase Auth service for successful responses. They do not require an existing bearer access token in the request. Refresh requires the private refresh token in its body.\n\n### A. `POST /api/v1/auth/register`\n\nAuthentication: none. Run before login when creating a new test account. Use an email you control; `student-a@example.com` below is a placeholder.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"email\": \"student-a@example.com\",\n  \"password\": \"REPLACE_WITH_PRIVATE_TEST_PASSWORD\",\n  \"username\": \"manual_student_a\",\n  \"full_name\": \"Manual Student A\"\n}\n```\n\nExpected success: **201**, `AuthResponse`. When email confirmation is required:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user\": {\n    \"id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\n    \"email\": \"student-a@example.com\"\n  },\n  \"session\": null,\n  \"confirmation_required\": true\n}\n```\n\nWhen confirmation is not required and a verified session is returned, the response has the session shape shown under login. No application profile is created until a verified session is available. New verified onboarding creates the profile and default preferences; existing profile details are preserved. If the optional username is already claimed, onboarding can leave it null rather than blocking login.\n\nFailures: 422 for malformed email, password shorter than 8 or longer than 1024 characters, invalid profile text, or extra fields; 400 when Supabase rejects registration; 429 for provider rate limits; 502 for provider failure/unverifiable returned session; 503 for missing Auth configuration/provider connectivity or required database unavailability. A missing Auth user in the configured application database can produce 409 during onboarding. Duplicate signup behavior depends on Supabase confirmation/privacy settings; do not assume every repeated signup returns 409.\n\n### B. `POST /api/v1/auth/login`\n\nAuthentication: none. Run after any required confirmation.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"email\": \"student-a@example.com\",\n  \"password\": \"REPLACE_WITH_PRIVATE_TEST_PASSWORD\"\n}\n```\n\nExpected success: **200**:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user\": {\n    \"id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\n    \"email\": \"student-a@example.com\"\n  },\n  \"session\": {\n    \"access_token\": \"REPLACE_WITH_ACCESS_TOKEN\",\n    \"refresh_token\": \"REPLACE_WITH_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\n    \"token_type\": \"bearer\",\n    \"expires_in\": 3600,\n    \"expires_at\": 1794823200\n  },\n  \"confirmation_required\": false\n}\n```\n\nUUIDs, tokens, expiration values, and email come from your real session; `expires_at` can be null. Login accepts only email/password, not registration profile fields. It provisions a missing own profile/default preferences after verification.\n\nFailures: 401 for incorrect credentials or an unconfirmed/rejected account; 422 for invalid email, empty password, password over 1024 characters, or extra fields; 429/502/503 for provider/configuration/dependency failures; 409 if onboarding cannot find the matching Auth user in the application database.\n\nOptional PowerShell login without displaying the password/token response:\n\n```powershell\n$manualBase = 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1'\n$manualEmail = Read-Host 'Your confirmed test account email'\n$manualSecret = Read-Host 'Test account password' -AsSecureString\n$manualPassword = [System.Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', $manualSecret).Password\n$manualLoginBody = @{ email = $manualEmail; password = $manualPassword } | ConvertTo-Json\n$manualLogin = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri \"$manualBase/auth/login\" `\n    -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $manualLoginBody\n$manualAccessToken = $manualLogin.session.access_token\n$manualRefreshToken = $manualLogin.session.refresh_token\n$manualHeaders = @{ Authorization = 'Bearer ' + $manualAccessToken }\nRemove-Variable manualPassword, manualLoginBody, manualSecret\n```\n\n### C. `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`\n\nAuthentication: no bearer token required; provide the current refresh token. Run after successful login and replace the saved tokens before proceeding to CRUD.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"refresh_token\": \"REPLACE_WITH_CURRENT_REFRESH_TOKEN\"\n}\n```\n\nExpected success: **200**, the same `AuthResponse` shape as login, with a verified session and rotated token values. Save the newly returned access and refresh tokens. Refresh can succeed without application database availability; it does not perform database onboarding.\n\nFailures: 422 for an empty refresh token, over 4096 characters, or extra fields; 401 for a rejected/expired/revoked refresh token; 429 for rate limits; 502 for invalid provider response/unverifiable session; 503 for missing Auth configuration or unavailable provider. Do not assume immediate reuse of an older token always fails; Supabase can apply a reuse grace interval.\n\nPowerShell:\n\n```powershell\n$manualRefreshBody = @{ refresh_token = $manualRefreshToken } | ConvertTo-Json\n$manualRefreshed = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri \"$manualBase/auth/refresh\" `\n    -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $manualRefreshBody\n$manualAccessToken = $manualRefreshed.session.access_token\n$manualRefreshToken = $manualRefreshed.session.refresh_token\n$manualHeaders = @{ Authorization = 'Bearer ' + $manualAccessToken }\nRemove-Variable manualRefreshBody\n```\n\n## 7. Configure authentication in Swagger\n\n1. Click **Authorize** near the top of Swagger.\n2. In the HTTP bearer input, paste only your actual access token. Do not include the word `Bearer`; Swagger adds it to the header.\n3. Click **Authorize**, then **Close**.\n4. Execute `GET /api/v1/profiles/me` to establish/retrieve your own profile before creating Tasks/Events.\n\nThe HTTP header used by PowerShell or another client is:\n\n```text\nAuthorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_ACCESS_TOKEN\n```\n\nAfter refresh, replace the token in Swagger too. Use **Logout** inside the authorization dialog to test missing authentication or change users. Reauthorize when the access token expires. Never paste the refresh token or project public key into the bearer input.\n\nProtected operations below require this verified access token and the matching configured database. With no bearer token, they return 401. With valid-looking credentials but missing Auth/database configuration, they can return 503 instead; do not interpret that as an ownership result.\n\n## 8. Profile and preferences\n\nRun these before scheduling inputs. All four routes require User A's real bearer access token.\n\n| Order | Method/path | Example request body | Expected success | Expected failures |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `GET /api/v1/profiles/me` | None | 200 `ProfileRead` below; a missing own profile is provisioned idempotently | 401 invalid/missing/expired token; 409 missing matching Auth user; 503 configuration/DB unavailable |\n| 2 | `PATCH /api/v1/profiles/me` | `{\"full_name\":\"Manual Student A Updated\",\"username\":\"manual_student_a\"}` | 200 complete updated `ProfileRead` | 422 invalid/extra/ownership fields; 409 username conflict; 401/503 authentication/dependency errors |\n| 3 | `GET /api/v1/preferences/me` | None | 200 `PreferencesRead` below | 401; 409 profile/onboarding dependency conflict; 503 configuration/DB unavailable |\n| 4 | `PATCH /api/v1/preferences/me` | `{\"timezone\":\"Africa/Cairo\",\"notifications_enabled\":true,\"preferred_work_start\":\"09:00:00\",\"preferred_work_end\":\"17:00:00\"}` | 200 complete updated `PreferencesRead` | 422 invalid timezone/boolean/combined work interval/extra fields; 401/409/503 as above |\n\nExample `ProfileRead`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\n  \"username\": \"manual_student_a\",\n  \"full_name\": \"Manual Student A Updated\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:05:00Z\"\n}\n```\n\nExample `PreferencesRead` after PATCH:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"preference_id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004\",\n  \"user_id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\n  \"timezone\": \"Africa/Cairo\",\n  \"notifications_enabled\": true,\n  \"preferred_work_start\": \"09:00:00\",\n  \"preferred_work_end\": \"17:00:00\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:05:00Z\"\n}\n```\n\nFor a newly created profile, preferences initially use UTC, notifications false, and both work endpoints null. Profile username/full_name can be cleared with null. Username is case-sensitive unique, at most 100 characters, and cannot be blank or padded; full_name is at most 200 and cannot be whitespace-only.\n\nPreferences timezone must be supported IANA/UTC. Notifications must be a JSON boolean. Work endpoints use local whole-second times without offsets. Both must be null or both supplied and unequal; an earlier end means an overnight window. To clear the window, PATCH both fields together:\n\n```json\n{\"preferred_work_start\":null,\"preferred_work_end\":null}\n```\n\nAfter each PATCH, run the corresponding GET and check persistence. Save your returned profile `id` privately for the two-user check.\n\nPowerShell GET example:\n\n```powershell\nInvoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri \"$manualBase/profiles/me\" -Headers $manualHeaders\nInvoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri \"$manualBase/preferences/me\" -Headers $manualHeaders\n```\n\n## 9. Task CRUD\n\nEvery Task endpoint requires a real bearer access token. First complete profile retrieval. Save the returned `task_id`; replace `{task_id}` with that actual UUID, without braces.\n\n### Request examples\n\nFLEXIBLE creation body:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"title\": \"Manual A assignment\",\n  \"task_type\": \"FLEXIBLE\",\n  \"estimated_duration_minutes\": 60,\n  \"category\": \"STUDY\",\n  \"priority\": 5,\n  \"deadline\": \"2026-11-20T18:00:00+02:00\",\n  \"context\": \"Manual testing chapter\"\n}\n```\n\nFIXED creation body for a second Task:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"title\": \"Manual A fixed study session\",\n  \"task_type\": \"FIXED\",\n  \"estimated_duration_minutes\": 60,\n  \"category\": \"STUDY\",\n  \"priority\": 3,\n  \"fixed_start_at\": \"2026-11-16T09:00:00+02:00\",\n  \"fixed_end_at\": \"2026-11-16T10:00:00+02:00\"\n}\n```\n\nDates can be adjusted for your manual session; a past deadline is permitted by the implementation. Timestamps need UTC offsets and are returned in UTC. Categories are `STUDY`, `WORK`, `PERSONAL`, `HEALTH`, `MEETING`; importance is the integer field `priority`, 1-5. Estimated duration is a positive integer, at most 2147483647 minutes. FIXED endpoints must be present with end after start. FLEXIBLE endpoints must be null/omitted. Duration is not required to equal the fixed interval length.\n\n### Endpoint sequence\n\n| Order | Method/path | Example request body | Expected success | Expected failures |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `POST /api/v1/tasks` | FLEXIBLE or FIXED body above | 201 complete `TaskRead` below | 422 invalid type/category/priority/duration/interval or forbidden fields; 409 missing profile; 401/503 authentication/dependency errors |\n| 2 | `GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` | None | 200 complete stored `TaskRead` | 404 missing/other-user ID; 422 malformed UUID; 401/503 |\n| 3 | `GET /api/v1/tasks` | None; query example `?limit=2&offset=0&category=STUDY` | 200 page of complete `TaskRead` objects | 422 invalid query values/bounds; 401/503 |\n| 4 | `PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` | `{\"title\":\"Manual A assignment updated\",\"priority\":4}` | 200 complete updated `TaskRead` | 404 missing/other-user ID; 422 invalid merged record/UUID/forbidden fields; 401/503 |\n| Final cleanup | `DELETE /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` | None | 204, empty body | 404 missing/other-user/already deleted ID; 422 malformed UUID; 401/503 |\n\nExample `TaskRead` for the FLEXIBLE creation:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"title\": \"Manual A assignment\",\n  \"task_type\": \"FLEXIBLE\",\n  \"estimated_duration_minutes\": 60,\n  \"category\": \"STUDY\",\n  \"priority\": 5,\n  \"deadline\": \"2026-11-20T16:00:00Z\",\n  \"fixed_start_at\": null,\n  \"fixed_end_at\": null,\n  \"context\": \"Manual testing chapter\",\n  \"task_id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002\",\n  \"user_id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\n  \"status\": \"UNSCHEDULED\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\"\n}\n```\n\nGET and PATCH use this same full response shape; changed values and timestamps reflect your actual record. Status is always server-managed `UNSCHEDULED` in Sprint 1. Do not submit ID, owner, status, or timestamps.\n\nPATCH validates the combined stored/new record. For a FIXED Task, changing only its type to FLEXIBLE fails while stored fixed endpoints remain. This atomic switch succeeds:\n\n```json\n{\"task_type\":\"FLEXIBLE\",\"fixed_start_at\":null,\"fixed_end_at\":null}\n```\n\nOmitted fields stay unchanged; null clears nullable fields such as deadline/context. Required values cannot be set to null. After PATCH, GET the Task again. After final deletion, GET it again and expect 404.\n\nPowerShell creation example, using your existing `$manualHeaders`:\n\n```powershell\n$manualTaskBody = @{\n    title = 'Manual A assignment'\n    task_type = 'FLEXIBLE'\n    estimated_duration_minutes = 60\n    category = 'STUDY'\n    priority = 5\n} | ConvertTo-Json\n$manualTask = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri \"$manualBase/tasks\" `\n    -Headers $manualHeaders -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $manualTaskBody\n$manualTaskId = $manualTask.task_id\nInvoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri \"$manualBase/tasks/$manualTaskId\" -Headers $manualHeaders\n```\n\n## 10. Event CRUD: ONCE and WEEKLY\n\nEvery Event endpoint requires a real bearer access token. Lectures/work shifts are Events and do not create duplicate Tasks. Save each returned `event_id`; use actual UUIDs in path inputs.\n\n### ONCE creation body\n\n```json\n{\n  \"title\": \"Manual A lecture\",\n  \"category\": \"STUDY\",\n  \"location\": \"Room 2\",\n  \"recurrence_type\": \"ONCE\",\n  \"start_at\": \"2026-11-16T09:00:00+02:00\",\n  \"end_at\": \"2026-11-16T10:00:00+02:00\"\n}\n```\n\nONCE is the default if recurrence_type is omitted. End must follow start, timestamps need offsets, and weekly fields must be null/omitted.\n\n### WEEKLY timetable creation body\n\n```json\n{\n  \"title\": \"Manual A weekly work shift\",\n  \"category\": \"WORK\",\n  \"location\": \"Office\",\n  \"recurrence_type\": \"WEEKLY\",\n  \"recurrence_first_date\": \"2026-11-16\",\n  \"recurrence_until_date\": \"2026-12-28\",\n  \"recurrence_start_time\": \"22:00:00\",\n  \"recurrence_end_time\": \"06:00:00\",\n  \"recurrence_end_day_offset\": 1,\n  \"recurrence_timezone\": \"Africa/Cairo\",\n  \"weekday\": 1\n}\n```\n\nNovember 16, 2026 is Monday, ISO weekday 1. If you change the first date, update weekday to match or omit weekday and let the backend derive it. ISO weekdays run Monday=1 through Sunday=7. For a lecture on Monday and Wednesday, create two separate weekly rules.\n\nWEEKLY requires first date, local whole-second start/end times, end-day offset, and timezone. Until is optional but cannot precede first date. Use offset 0 for a same-day interval with end later than start; offset 1 supports overnight intervals. ONCE endpoints must be null/omitted. Changing preferences timezone does not change a rule's stored timezone.\n\n### Endpoint sequence\n\n| Order | Method/path | Example request body | Expected success | Expected failures |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `POST /api/v1/events` | ONCE body above | 201 complete ONCE `EventRead` below | 422 invalid interval/category/shape or forbidden fields; 409 missing profile; 401/503 authentication/dependency errors |\n| 2 | `POST /api/v1/events` | WEEKLY body above | 201 complete WEEKLY `EventRead` below | 422 missing rule fields, invalid dates/weekday/timezone/DST endpoints or mixed shapes; 409/401/503 as above |\n| 3 | `GET /api/v1/events/{event_id}` | None | 200 complete stored `EventRead` | 404 missing/other-user ID; 422 malformed UUID; 401/503 |\n| 4 | `GET /api/v1/events` | None; query example `?limit=2&recurrence_type=WEEKLY` | 200 page of complete `EventRead` objects | 422 invalid pagination/category/recurrence query values; 401/503 |\n| 5 | `PATCH /api/v1/events/{event_id}` | `{\"title\":\"Manual A lecture updated\",\"location\":\"Room 3\"}` | 200 complete updated `EventRead` | 404 missing/other-user ID; 422 invalid merged rule/interval/UUID/forbidden fields; 401/503 |\n| Final cleanup | `DELETE /api/v1/events/{event_id}` | None | 204, empty body; entire stored rule if WEEKLY | 404 missing/other-user/already deleted ID; 422 malformed UUID; 401/503 |\n\nExample ONCE `EventRead`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"title\": \"Manual A lecture\",\n  \"category\": \"STUDY\",\n  \"location\": \"Room 2\",\n  \"recurrence_type\": \"ONCE\",\n  \"start_at\": \"2026-11-16T07:00:00Z\",\n  \"end_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\n  \"recurrence_first_date\": null,\n  \"recurrence_until_date\": null,\n  \"recurrence_start_time\": null,\n  \"recurrence_end_time\": null,\n  \"recurrence_end_day_offset\": null,\n  \"recurrence_timezone\": null,\n  \"event_id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003\",\n  \"user_id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\n  \"source\": \"MANUAL\",\n  \"status\": \"SAVED\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\n  \"weekday\": null\n}\n```\n\nExample WEEKLY `EventRead`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"title\": \"Manual A weekly work shift\",\n  \"category\": \"WORK\",\n  \"location\": \"Office\",\n  \"recurrence_type\": \"WEEKLY\",\n  \"start_at\": null,\n  \"end_at\": null,\n  \"recurrence_first_date\": \"2026-11-16\",\n  \"recurrence_until_date\": \"2026-12-28\",\n  \"recurrence_start_time\": \"22:00:00\",\n  \"recurrence_end_time\": \"06:00:00\",\n  \"recurrence_end_day_offset\": 1,\n  \"recurrence_timezone\": \"Africa/Cairo\",\n  \"event_id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005\",\n  \"user_id\": \"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\",\n  \"source\": \"MANUAL\",\n  \"status\": \"SAVED\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-11-16T08:00:00Z\",\n  \"weekday\": 1\n}\n```\n\nGET/PATCH return these same complete shapes, with actual IDs/values/timestamps. Source/status stay server-managed MANUAL/SAVED. No generated occurrences or exception records are returned.\n\nPATCH applies to the entire weekly rule. Changing only the type while keeping incompatible stored fields fails. Example conversion of an existing ONCE Event to WEEKLY:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"recurrence_type\": \"WEEKLY\",\n  \"start_at\": null,\n  \"end_at\": null,\n  \"recurrence_first_date\": \"2026-11-16\",\n  \"recurrence_start_time\": \"09:00:00\",\n  \"recurrence_end_time\": \"10:00:00\",\n  \"recurrence_end_day_offset\": 0,\n  \"recurrence_timezone\": \"Africa/Cairo\",\n  \"weekday\": 1\n}\n```\n\nTo convert WEEKLY to ONCE, provide valid start_at/end_at and set all weekly rule fields, including weekday, to null in the same PATCH. After every PATCH, GET the record. After final deletion, GET it and expect 404.\n\n## 11. Pagination and filtering\n\nRequires a real bearer token and manually created records. Create at least three matching Tasks and three matching Events before checking multiple pages. Keep records unchanged while comparing pages.\n\nBoth list endpoints return this page structure; this is an exact empty-page example:\n\n```json\n{\"items\":[],\"limit\":2,\"offset\":0,\"has_more\":false}\n```\n\nFor non-empty pages, `items` contains full TaskRead or EventRead objects shown above. There is no total/count field. Default limit is 50; allowed limit is 1-100 and offset 0-1000000. `has_more` indicates whether another item exists after this page. For the next page, increase offset by the number of returned items.\n\n| Method/path example | Authentication/body | Expected result/failure |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GET /api/v1/tasks?limit=2&offset=0` | Bearer; no body | 200, at most two own Tasks; has_more true if more matching records exist |\n| `GET /api/v1/tasks?limit=2&offset=2` | Bearer; no body | 200 next page; no overlap while data remains unchanged |\n| `GET /api/v1/tasks?category=STUDY&task_type=FLEXIBLE&priority=5` | Bearer; no body | 200 own Tasks matching all filters |\n| `GET /api/v1/tasks?deadline_from=2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&deadline_to=2026-11-21T23:59:59Z` | Bearer; no body | 200 matching Tasks; deadline boundaries are inclusive and exclude null deadlines |\n| `GET /api/v1/events?limit=2&offset=0&category=WORK&recurrence_type=WEEKLY` | Bearer; no body | 200 matching own stored rules; one record per rule, not per occurrence |\n| `GET /api/v1/events?recurrence_type=ONCE` | Bearer; no body | 200 own ONCE Events only |\n\nTask ordering is deadline ascending, null last, then task_id. ONCE-filtered Event ordering is start_at/event_id; WEEKLY-filtered ordering is recurrence_first_date/event_id; unfiltered Event ordering is created_at/event_id. An empty result is 200, not 404.\n\nInvalid pagination/category/type/priority/deadline inputs return 422; missing/invalid authentication returns 401; unavailable dependencies can return 503. Query priority is a number 1-5. Use UTC `Z` in URL timestamps, or URL-encode a plus offset as `%2B`; Swagger handles query encoding.\n\nPowerShell list example:\n\n```powershell\nInvoke-RestMethod -Method Get `\n    -Uri \"$manualBase/tasks?limit=2&offset=0&category=STUDY\" -Headers $manualHeaders\n```\n\n## 12. Invalid inputs and expected errors\n\nChange one input at a time. Confirm failures leave the existing record unchanged by GETting it again. Do not deliberately interrupt databases, corrupt tokens, or flood the provider to manufacture infrastructure failures.\n\n### Checks possible without real Supabase credentials\n\n| Request/action | Expected result |\n|---|---|\n| Swagger Logout, then `GET /api/v1/profiles/me`, `/preferences/me`, `/tasks`, or `/events` | 401 and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` |\n| `POST /api/v1/auth/register` with `{\"email\":\"bad\",\"password\":\"short\"}` | 422 schema validation before contacting Auth |\n| `POST /api/v1/auth/login` with `{\"email\":\"bad\",\"password\":\"\"}` | 422 schema validation before contacting Auth |\n| `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` with `{\"refresh_token\":\"\"}` | 422 schema validation before contacting Auth |\n\nProtected validation checks below should use a valid real token; without it, authentication/dependency errors can happen before field validation.\n\n### Authenticated input checks\n\n| Endpoint/action | Invalid example | Expected result |\n|---|---|---|\n| `PATCH /profiles/me` | `{\"id\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006\"}` | 422 forbidden field |\n| `PATCH /profiles/me` | `{\"full_name\":\"   \"}` or `{\"username\":\" padded \"}` | 422 |\n| `PATCH /profiles/me` | A username already owned by the other manual account | 409; previous profile remains unchanged |\n| `PATCH /preferences/me` | `{\"timezone\":\"Invalid/Zone\"}` or `{\"notifications_enabled\":\"yes\"}` | 422 |\n| `PATCH /preferences/me` | Clear only one endpoint of a stored non-null work window | 422 merged interval validation |\n| `POST /tasks` | Valid Task body changed to priority 0/6, duration 0, category OTHER, or title whitespace-only | 422 |\n| `POST /tasks` | Add `\"user_id\"`, `\"status\"`, generated ID, or timestamps to a valid body | 422 |\n| `POST /tasks` | FIXED without both endpoints; or FLEXIBLE with a fixed endpoint | 422 |\n| `PATCH /tasks/{task_id}` | `{\"priority\":null}` | 422 required value cannot be null |\n| `POST /events` | ONCE end equal to/before start, or timestamps without offsets | 422 |\n| `POST /events` | WEEKLY until before first date; weekday not matching first date; missing timezone; negative day offset | 422 |\n| `POST /events` | Mix ONCE start_at/end_at with weekly fields | 422 |\n| `PATCH /events/{event_id}` | Add source/status/user_id, or leave an invalid combined interval | 422 |\n| Task/Event GET/PATCH/DELETE by ID | `not-a-uuid` as path input | 422 with a valid token |\n| Task/Event GET/PATCH/DELETE by ID | Well-formed UUID that does not exist, with an otherwise valid body where needed | 404 |\n| Either collection GET | limit=0/101, offset=-1/1000001, category=OTHER | 422 |\n| Task collection GET | Upper deadline bound earlier than lower bound | 422 |\n\nPath prefixes in this table are `/api/v1`.\n\nFor a manual DST rejection check, use a valid WEEKLY body with recurrence_timezone `America/New_York`, first date `2026-03-08`, weekday 7, start `02:30:00`, end `03:30:00`, and end-day offset 0; omit until. Expected 422 because the first start falls in the spring DST gap. An analogous first-date fold example is `2026-11-01`, weekday 7, start `01:30:00`, end `02:30:00`, offset 0: expected 422 for ambiguity.\n\nWeekly validation checks first and bounded final occurrence endpoints. It does not certify every intervening/future DST transition or expand occurrences. Later scheduling consumers must resolve each interpreted occurrence themselves.\n\nExample validation error shape:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": \"invalid_request\",\n    \"message\": \"Request validation failed\",\n    \"details\": [\n      {\n        \"field\": \"body.priority\",\n        \"message\": \"Input should be less than or equal to 5\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nAll backend errors use `error.code`, `error.message`, and `error.details` (an array, sometimes empty). Exact validation messages/field locations depend on the rejected rule. Other useful statuses:\n\n- 400: registration rejected by Auth.\n- 401: invalid/missing/expired bearer token, or rejected login/refresh credentials.\n- 404: absent or other-user Task/Event.\n- 409: uniqueness or profile/Auth-user dependency conflict.\n- 422: request or combined-record validation.\n- 429: Auth rate limit; honor Retry-After if present.\n- 502: failed/invalid/unverifiable Auth provider response.\n- 503: configuration, restricted runtime role, database, or Auth availability issue.\n- 500: unexpected backend error; record the route/status and sanitized response for investigation.\n\nInvalid bearer checks require working verifier configuration to establish a meaningful 401. With an incompatible signing algorithm, login can return 502 for an unverifiable upstream session, while protected requests reject its token with 401. Do not change security rules to make that token work.\n\n## 13. Verify two-user isolation\n\nThis requires two real accounts in the same configured Supabase project. Do not use administrator/service-role tokens for either account.\n\n1. With User A authorized, create at least one Task and one Event. Save their IDs and A's profile ID. Set a recognizable profile name/preferences value.\n2. Register/confirm/login User B. Log out A in Swagger and authorize using B's access token, or use separate normal/private browser sessions. Do not forge SQL identity claims or use a privileged role as the API runtime. Use the authenticated API to inspect your user's rows. Do not edit/delete existing records there. Legacy `anon` keys are only for compatibility. In Next.js, any `NEXT_PUBLIC_` env var is sent to the browser.\\r\\n  - **Use scoped personal access tokens for the Management API, CLI, and MCP server.** A classic personal access token carries the user's full account access, on every organization and project. For scripts, CI, and agents, have the user create a scoped token limited to the organizations, projects, and permissions the task needs. The [personal access tokens guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/personal-access-tokens.md) lists the permission each Management API endpoint and MCP tool requires. Look permissions up there rather than guessing.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **RLS, views, and privileged database code**\\r\\n  - **Views bypass RLS by default.** In Postgres 15 and above, use `CREATE VIEW ... WITH (security_invoker = true)`. In older versions of Postgres, protect your views by revoking access from the `anon` and `authenticated` roles, or by putting them in an unexposed schema.\\r\\n  - **UPDATE requires a SELECT policy.** In Postgres RLS, an UPDATE needs to first SELECT the row. Without a SELECT policy, updates silently return 0 rows â€” no error, just no change.\\r\\n  - **`auth.role()` is deprecated â€” use the `TO` clause instead.** Supabase has deprecated `auth.role()` in favour of specifying the target role directly on the policy with `TO authenticated` or `TO anon`. Beyond deprecation, `auth.role() = 'authenticated'` breaks silently when anonymous sign-ins are enabled, because anonymous users carry the `authenticated` Postgres role and pass the check regardless of whether the user is genuinely signed in.\\r\\n    ```sql\\r\\n    -- Deprecated (do not use)\\r\\n    create policy \\\"example\\\" on table_name for select\\r\\n    using ( auth.role() = 'authenticated' );\\r\\n    ```\\r\\n  - **`TO authenticated` alone is authentication without authorization (BOLA / IDOR).** Using `TO authenticated` only checks the role â€” it does not restrict which rows a user can access. The correct pattern combines `TO authenticated` with an ownership predicate in `USING`:\\r\\n    ```sql\\r\\n    create policy \\\"example\\\" on table_name for select\\r\\n    to authenticated\\r\\n    using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\\r\\n    ```\\r\\n  - **UPDATE policies require both `USING` and `WITH CHECK`.** Without `WITH CHECK`, a user can reassign a row's `user_id` to another user:\\r\\n    ```sql\\r\\n    create policy \\\"example\\\" on table_name for update\\r\\n    to authenticated\\r\\n    using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id )\\r\\n    with check ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\\r\\n    ```\\r\\n  - **`SECURITY DEFINER` functions bypass RLS.** A `SECURITY DEFINER` function runs with its creator's privileges â€” typically a role with `bypassrls` (e.g., `postgres`). Never add `SECURITY DEFINER` to resolve a permission error; it silently removes access control without fixing the underlying cause. Prefer `SECURITY INVOKER`.\\r\\n  - **`SECURITY DEFINER` functions in `public` are callable by all roles.** Postgres grants `EXECUTE` to `PUBLIC` by default for every new function, so any `SECURITY DEFINER` function in `public` is a public API endpoint callable by `anon` and `authenticated` (which inherit from `PUBLIC`) without any additional grant. When `SECURITY DEFINER` is genuinely needed (e.g., bypassing RLS on an internal lookup table), keep the function in a non-exposed schema, always include an `auth.uid()` check in the function body, and run `supabase db advisors` after making changes.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Storage access control**\\r\\n  - **Storage upsert requires INSERT + SELECT + UPDATE.** Granting only INSERT allows new uploads but file replacement (upsert) silently fails. You need all three.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Dependency and supply-chain security**\\r\\n  - **Always pin package versions and commit lockfiles** when installing Supabase packages (`supabase-js`, `@supabase/ssr`, `supabase-py`, etc.). See the [npm security guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/security/npm-security.md) for the full checklist.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor any security concern not covered above, fetch the Supabase product security index: `https://supabase.com/docs/guides/security/product-security.md`\\r\\n\\r\\n## Supabase CLI\\r\\n\\r\\nAlways discover commands via `--help` â€” never guess. When empty, the API gateway and all services operate in legacy-only mode: `sb_publishable` and `sb_secret` API keys are not configured.\\\\n\\\\n| Environment variable (existing and new) | Type             | Description                                                                                                                           |\\\\n| --------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\\\n| `JWT_SECRET`                            | Symmetric secret | **Existing:** Shared secret for signing and verifying HS256 JWTs. Used by multiple services.                                          |\\\\n| `ANON_KEY`                              | HS256 JWT        | **Existing:** Legacy client-side API key. Embedded JWT with `role: \\\\\\\"anon\\\\\\\"`.                                                           |\\\\n| `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`                      | HS256 JWT        | **Existing:** Legacy server-side API key. Embedded JWT with `role: \\\\\\\"service_role\\\\\\\"`.                                                   |\\\\n| `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`              | Opaque           | **New:** Short random key with checksum. Replaces `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` for **server-side** use.                                         |\\\\n| `JWT_KEYS`                              | JSON array       | **New:** JSON array of signing JWKs containing the new asymmetric key pair and the legacy symmetric key. Used by Auth to sign tokens. |\\\\n| `JWT_JWKS`                              | JWKS (JSON)      | **New:** Contains the new public key and the legacy symmetric key. Used by PostgREST, Realtime, and Storage to verify tokens.         |\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Differences from the Supabase platform\\\\n\\\\n*   **One key per role.** Self-hosted Supabase supports a single `sb_publishable` and a single `sb_secret`. The platform allows creating multiple `sb_` keys per project.\\\\n*   **No checksum validation.** The opaque keys use the same format as the platform (`sb_publishable_<random>_<checksum>`), but the API gateway does not validate the checksum. Keys are matched as opaque strings by the API gateway.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Backward compatibility\\\\n\\\\nThe new authentication configuration is fully backward compatible:\\\\n\\\\n*   **The API Gateway accepts both key types simultaneously.** You can migrate clients incrementally - some using legacy API keys, others using the new ones.\\\\n*   **JWKS includes the symmetric key.** `JWT_JWKS` contains both the EC public key (for verifying new ES256 tokens) and the legacy `JWT_SECRET` as a symmetric JWK (for verifying old HS256 tokens). Services that receive `JWT_JWKS` can verify both token types.\\\\n*   **No database changes required.** The asymmetric key system operates entirely at the API gateway and service configuration layer.\\\\n\\\\n<Admonition type=\\\\\\\"caution\\\\\\\">\\\\n  When `JWT_KEYS` is set, Auth will start signing new user session JWTs with the new asymmetric ES256 key pair. Make sure all services that verify tokens (PostgREST, Realtime, Storage) are configured with `JWT_JWKS` so they can verify both the new ES256 and legacy HS256 tokens.\\\\n</Admonition>\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Rotating the new API keys\\\\n\\\\nIf your new API keys are compromised or you want to rotate them periodically, you can regenerate `sb_publishable` and `sb_secret` without touching the asymmetric key pair:\\\\n\\\\n```sh\\\\nsh utils/rotate-new-api-keys.sh --update-env\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nAfter rotating, restart services and update your client applications with the new keys:\\\\n\\\\n```sh\\\\ndocker compose down && docker compose up -d\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n<Admonition type=\\\\\\\"note\\\\\\\">\\\\n  Rotating new API keys does not invalidate existing user sessions. User session JWTs issued by Auth are unaffected because they are verified using the asymmetric key pair, which remains unchanged.\\\\n</Admonition>\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Regenerating asymmetric key pair\\\\n\\\\nIf the EC private key is compromised or you need to regenerate everything:\\\\n\\\\n```sh\\\\nsh utils/add-new-auth-keys.sh --update-env\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThis generates a new EC P-256 key pair, new JWKS, new asymmetric JWTs, and new `sb_` API keys. After updating `.env` and restarting services:\\\\n\\\\n*   New user session tokens will be signed with the new EC key.\\\\n*   Existing user session tokens signed with the old EC key will fail verification. Users will need to sign in again.\\\\n*   Existing user session tokens signed with the legacy symmetric key (`JWT_SECRET`) will continue to work, since `JWT_SECRET` hasn't changed and is still included in the new JWKS.\\\\n\\\\n<Admonition type=\\\\\\\"danger\\\\\\\">\\\\n  Regenerating asymmetric keys invalidates all ES256 user sessions. Plan a maintenance window if your users have active sessions.\\\\n</Admonition>\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## How it works\\\\n\\\\nBelow are a few notes on the details of the new authentication architecture.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### What client SDK sends\\\\n\\\\nEvery request via `supabase-js` includes two headers:\\\\n\\\\n*   `apikey` - the API key (`sb_` or legacy JWT)\\\\n*   `Authorization` - when unauthenticated, the client SDK copies the API key here (`Bearer sb_publishable_xxx` or `Bearer eyJ...`). When authenticated, this contains the user session JWT minted by Auth.\\\\n\\\\nFor **Realtime WebSocket** connections, the API key is sent as a `?apikey=` query parameter in the upgrade URL instead of an `apikey` header.\\\\n\\\\n**Storage** and **Edge Functions** accept requests without an API key. These services handle their own authentication.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Kong API gateway routing\\\\n\\\\nKong is configured with two consumers that each accept both the legacy and new API keys:\\\\n\\\\n<NamedCodeBlock name=\\\\\\\"volumes/api/kong.yml\\\\\\\">\\\\n  ```yaml name=volumes/api/kong.yml\\\\n  consumers:\\\\n    - username: anon\\\\n      keyauth_credentials:\\\\n        - key: $SUPABASE_ANON_KEY # legacy HS256 JWT (ANON_KEY)\\\\n        - key: $SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY # new opaque key (omitted when not configured)\\\\n    - username: service_role\\\\n      keyauth_credentials:\\\\n        - key: $SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY # legacy HS256 JWT (SERVICE_ROLE_KEY)\\\\n        - key: $SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY # new opaque key (omitted when not configured)\\\\n  ```\\\\n</NamedCodeBlock>\\\\n\\\\nWhen new API keys have not been added yet, the `kong-entrypoint.sh` script removes the empty credential entries before Kong loads the config.\\\\n\\\\nTo assist with the authorization flows a specialized configuration in `kong.yml` substitutes internal, gateway-level-only pre-signed JWTs for `sb_publishable` and `sb_secret` API keys. These pre-signed JWTs are also auto-configured in `.env` but **should not** be used in any application code.\\\\n\\\\n| Route                | Service              | API key required | Header substitution |\\\\n| -------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------- |\\\\n| `/auth/v1/*`         | Auth                 | Yes              | `Authorization`     |\\\\n| `/rest/v1/*`         | PostgREST            | Yes              | `Authorization`     |\\\\n| `/graphql/v1`        | PostgREST            | Yes              | `Authorization`     |\\\\n| `/realtime/v1/api/*` | Realtime (REST)      | Yes              | `Authorization`     |\\\\n| `/realtime/v1/*`     | Realtime (WebSocket) | Yes              | `x-api-key`         |\\\\n| `/storage/v1/*`      | Storage              | No               | `Authorization`     |\\\\n| `/functions/v1/*`    | Edge Functions       | No               | -                   |\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Request flows\\\\n\\\\nThe API gateway (Kong) configuration has the logic to decide what `Authorization` header the upstream service, such as Auth, receives. The logic handles two cases: requests that only carry an API key (no user session), and requests that carry a user session JWT.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n#### Unauthenticated requests (API key only, no user session JWT)\\\\n\\\\nWhen the client sends only an `apikey` header with the API key (no `Authorization` header), or also the API key duplicated in `Authorization` by `supabase-js`:\\\\n\\\\n1.  The client sends `apikey: sb_publishable_xxx` (or legacy `apikey: eyJ...`).\\\\n2.  The API gateway checks the key and identifies the consumer (`anon` or `service_role`).\\\\n3.  The API gateway inspects the `Authorization` header. Since it is either absent or starts with `Bearer sb_` (an opaque key, not a session JWT), the plugin replaces it:\\\\n    *   **The new `sb_` key:** `Authorization` header is set to the internal pre-signed ES256 JWT that corresponds to the role.\\\\n    *   **The Legacy JWT key:** `Authorization` header is set to the legacy HS256 JWT (the `apikey` value is copied as-is).\\\\n4.  The upstream service receives a valid JWT in `Authorization` and verifies it using `JWT_JWKS` (or `JWT_SECRET`).\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n#### Authenticated requests (user session JWT)\\\\n\\\\nWhen the client has previously signed in through Auth and has a valid user session JWT token:\\\\n\\\\n1.  The client sends `Authorization: Bearer eyJ...` (a JWT session token from Auth) alongside `apikey: sb_publishable_xxx` (or legacy `apikey: eyJ...`).\\\\n2.  The API gateway checks the API key and identifies the consumer.\\\\n3.  The API gateway inspects the `Authorization` header. Since it exists and does **not** start with `Bearer sb_` (it's a real JWT, not an `sb_` API key), the plugin **passes it through unchanged**. This works the same way regardless of whether the `apikey` is a new `sb_` key or a legacy JWT - the gateway only looks at the `Authorization` header to decide whether a user session is present.\\\\n4.  The upstream service verifies the session JWT. If Auth signed it with ES256 (when `JWT_KEYS` is configured), verification uses the EC public key. If Auth signed it with HS256 (legacy), verification uses the symmetric key. Both keys are available in `JWT_JWKS`.\\\\n\\\\nThe `request-transformer` expression in `kong.yml` implements this as a single Lua conditional:\\\\n\\\\n```lua\\\\n-- Pseudocode for the Authorization header logic:\\\\nif authorization exists AND does not start with \\\\\\\"Bearer sb_\\\\\\\" then\\\\n  -- User session JWT: pass through unchanged\\\\n  keep authorization\\\\nelseif apikey matches secret key then\\\\n  -- Replace with pre-signed service_role ES256 JWT\\\\n  set authorization = \\\\\\\"Bearer <service_role ES256 JWT>\\\\\\\"\\\\nelseif apikey matches publishable key then\\\\n  -- Replace with pre-signed anon ES256 JWT\\\\n  set authorization = \\\\\\\"Bearer <anon ES256 JWT>\\\\\\\"\\\\nelse\\\\n  -- Legacy JWT key: copy apikey as authorization\\\\n  set authorization = apikey\\\\nend\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Additional resources\\\\n\\\\n*   [Understanding API keys](/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys) - This is the recommended approach for most applications:\\\\n\\\\n```ts index.ts\\\\nimport { createClient } from 'npm:@supabase/supabase-js@2'\\\\n\\\\nDeno.serve(async (req) => {\\\\n  try {\\\\n    const supabase = createClient(\\\\n      Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL') ?? '',\\\\n      Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY') ?? '',\\\\n      { global: { headers: { Authorization: req.headers.get('Authorization')! } } }\\\\n    )\\\\n\\\\n    const { data, error } = await supabase.from('countries').select('*')\\\\n\\\\n    if (error) {\\\\n      throw error\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ data }), {\\\\n      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\\\\n      status: 200,\\\\n    })\\\\n  } catch (err) {\\\\n    return new Response(String(err?.message ?? err), { status: 500 })\\\\n  }\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThis enables:\\\\n\\\\n*   Automatic Row Level Security enforcement\\\\n*   Built-in JSON serialization\\\\n*   Consistent error handling\\\\n*   TypeScript support for database schema\\\\n\\\\n***\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Using a Postgres client\\\\n\\\\nBecause Edge Functions are a server-side technology, it's safe to connect directly to your database using any popular Postgres client. This means you can run raw SQL from your Edge Functions.\\\\n\\\\nHere is how you can connect to the database using Deno Postgres driver and run raw SQL. Check out the [full example](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/tree/master/examples/edge-functions/supabase/functions/postgres-on-the-edge).\\\\n\\\\n<CodeSampleWrapper source=\\\\\\\"https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/edge-functions/supabase/functions/postgres-on-the-edge/index.ts\\\\\\\">\\\\n  ```typescript\\\\n  import { Pool } from 'https://deno.land/x/postgres@v0.17.0/mod.ts'\\\\n\\\\n  // Create a database pool with one connection.\\\\n  const pool = new Pool(\\\\n    {\\\\n      tls: { enabled: false },\\\\n      database: 'postgres',\\\\n      hostname: Deno.env.get('DB_HOSTNAME'),\\\\n      user: Deno.env.get('DB_USER'),\\\\n      port: 6543,\\\\n      password: Deno.env.get('DB_PASSWORD'),\\\\n    },\\\\n    1\\\\n  )\\\\n\\\\n  Deno.serve(async (_req) => {\\\\n    try {\\\\n      // Grab a connection from the pool\\\\n      const connection = await pool.connect()\\\\n\\\\n      try {\\\\n        // Run a query\\\\n        const result = await connection.queryObject`SELECT * FROM animals`\\\\n        const animals = result.rows // [{ id: 1, name: \\\\\\\"Lion\\\\\\\" }, ...]\\\\n\\\\n        // Encode the result as pretty printed JSON\\\\n        const body = JSON.stringify(\\\\n          animals,\\\\n          (_key, value) => (typeof value === 'bigint' ? value.toString() : value),\\\\n          2\\\\n        )\\\\n\\\\n        // Return the response with the correct content type header\\\\n        return new Response(body, {\\\\n          status: 200,\\\\n          headers: {\\\\n            'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',\\\\n          },\\\\n        })\\\\n      } finally {\\\\n        // Release the connection back into the pool\\\\n        connection.release()\\\\n      }\\\\n    } catch (err) {\\\\n      console.error(err)\\\\n      return new Response(String(err?.message ?? err), { status: 500 })\\\\n    }\\\\n  })\\\\n  ```\\\\n</CodeSampleWrapper>\\\\n\\\\n***\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Using Drizzle\\\\n\\\\nYou can use Drizzle together with [Postgres.js](https://github.com/porsager/postgres). Production\\\\n\\\\nDeployed edge functions are pre-configured to use SSL for connections to the Supabase database. You don't need to add any extra configurations.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Local development\\\\n\\\\nIf you want to use SSL connections during local development, follow these steps:\\\\n\\\\n1.
